title.zh: 卷26 志第21 百官上
title.raw: 卷26 志第21 百官上 Volume 26 Treatises 21: Government Offices 1

sentences.zh: 隋書卷二十六 志第二十一

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 26, Treatise 21
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 26, Treatise 21

sentences.zh: 百官上

translations.literal: Government Offices, Part 1
translations.idiomatic: Government Offices, Part 1

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天尊地卑，乾坤定矣，卑高既陳，貴賤位矣。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven is honored and earth is lowly; thus Qian and Kun are fixed. When high and low are set forth, noble and base take their places."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven is honored and earth is lowly; thus Qian and Kun are fixed. When high and low are set forth, noble and base take their places."

sentences.zh: 」是以聖人法乾坤以作則，因卑高以垂教，設官分職，錫珪胙土。

translations.literal: " Therefore the sage takes Heaven and Earth as his model to establish standards, and by high and low transmits instruction, establishing offices and dividing duties, bestowing jade tablets and enfeoffing with land.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the sage modeled himself on Heaven and Earth to establish standards, used rank to teach the people, set up offices and divided responsibilities, and granted jade tablets and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 由近以制遠，自中以統外。

translations.literal: From what is near to control what is distant; from the center to govern the outer regions.
translations.idiomatic: From the center he governed the periphery; from what was near he controlled what was far.

sentences.zh: 內則公卿大夫士，外則公侯伯子男。

translations.literal: Within were dukes, ministers, grand masters, and servicemen; without were dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons.
translations.idiomatic: Within the court were dukes, ministers, grand masters, and servicemen; beyond it were feudal lords ranked as duke, marquis, earl, viscount, and baron.

sentences.zh: 咸所以協和萬邦，平章百姓，允厘庶績，式敘彝倫。

translations.literal: All were to harmonize the myriad states, bring order to the common people, faithfully manage the multitude of tasks, and thereby arrange the constant norms.
translations.idiomatic: All this served to harmonize the myriad states, bring order to the people, manage affairs faithfully, and maintain the moral order of society.

sentences.zh: 其由來尚矣。

translations.literal: Its origins are indeed ancient.
translations.idiomatic: The origins of this system are indeed very old.

sentences.zh: 然古今異制，文質殊途。

translations.literal: Yet ancient and modern institutions differ, and the ornate and the plain follow separate paths.
translations.idiomatic: Yet institutions differ between past and present, and the ornate and the plain follow different paths.

sentences.zh: 或以龍表官，或以云紀職。

translations.literal: Some used dragons to designate offices; some used clouds to record duties.
translations.idiomatic: Some dynasties named offices after dragons; others recorded duties with cloud designations.

sentences.zh: 放勳即分命四子，重華乃爰置九官，夏倍于虞，殷倍于夏，周監二代，沿革不同。

translations.literal: Emperor Yao at once divided and appointed his four sons; Emperor Shun then established the Nine Ministers. Xia doubled Yu, Yin doubled Xia, and Zhou looked to both preceding dynasties—each changing and continuing in different ways.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao divided duties among his four sons; Emperor Shun established the Nine Ministers. Xia doubled the offices of Yu, Yin doubled those of Xia, and Zhou took both earlier dynasties as models—each changing and continuing in its own way.

sentences.zh: 其道既文，置官彌廣。

translations.literal: As the Way grew more refined, the offices established became ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: As civilization grew more refined, the number of offices steadily increased.

sentences.zh: 逮于戰國，戎馬交馳，雖時有變革，然猶承周制。

translations.literal: By the Warring States period, war-horses raced against one another; though there were changes from time to time, the Zhou system was still largely followed.
translations.idiomatic: By the Warring States period, armies clashed ceaselessly; though reforms occurred from time to time, the Zhou system was still largely retained.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇廢先王之典，焚百家之言，創立朝儀，事不師古，始罷封侯之制，立郡縣之官。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang abolished the institutions of the former kings, burned the writings of the hundred schools, established court ritual anew, and took no ancient models as his teachers. He first abolished the enfeoffment of marquises and established commandery and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang abolished the institutions of the former kings, burned the writings of the hundred schools, and created new court ritual without deferring to antiquity. He abolished enfeoffment and established commandery and county administration.

sentences.zh: 太尉主五兵，丞相總百揆，又置御史大夫，以貳於相。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant was in charge of the five armies; the Chancellor oversaw the hundred affairs; and the Grand Censor was also established as second to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant commanded the five armies; the Chancellor oversaw all government affairs; and the Grand Censor was established as the Chancellor's deputy.

sentences.zh: 自餘眾職，各有司存。

translations.literal: All remaining offices each had their own departments.
translations.idiomatic: All other offices each had their own departments.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖除暴甯亂，輕刑約法，而職官之制，因於嬴氏，其間同異，抑亦可知。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han suppressed violence and restored order, lightened punishments and simplified laws, yet the system of offices followed that of the House of Ying; the similarities and differences between them may still be discerned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han suppressed violence and restored order, lightened punishments and simplified laws, yet the system of offices followed that of Qin; the similarities and differences between them may still be discerned.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，聿遵前緒，唯廢丞相與御史大夫，而以三司綜理眾務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he followed the earlier pattern, abolishing only the Chancellor and Grand Censor and using the Three Excellencies to manage all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he largely followed earlier practice, abolishing only the Chancellor and Grand Censor and using the Three Excellencies to manage all affairs.

sentences.zh: 洎于叔世，事歸台閣，論道之官，備員而已。

translations.literal: By the late age, affairs passed to the Secretariat, and the officials who discussed the Way existed only to fill posts.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Han, real power passed to the Secretariat, and the high counselors existed only to fill posts.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉繼及，大抵略同，爰及宋、齊，亦無改作。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin followed in succession and were largely the same; extending to Song and Qi, there were no major changes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin followed in succession and were largely the same; through Song and Qi as well, there were no major reforms.

sentences.zh: 梁武受終，多循齊舊，然而定諸卿之位，各配四時，置戎秩之官，百有餘號。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang received the mandate, he largely followed Qi practice; yet he fixed the ranks of the various ministers, assigning each to one of the four seasons, and established military-rank offices numbering more than a hundred titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang received the mandate, he largely followed Qi practice; yet he fixed the ranks of the various ministers according to the four seasons and established more than a hundred military-rank offices.

sentences.zh: 陳氏繼梁，不失舊物。

translations.literal: The Chen house succeeded Liang and did not abandon the old institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen dynasty succeeded Liang and retained the old institutions.

sentences.zh: 高齊創業，亦遵後魏，台省位號，與江左稍殊，所有節文，備詳於志。

translations.literal: When Northern Qi was founded, it also followed Later Wei; the titles of the central offices differed somewhat from those of the south of the Yangzi, and the relevant regulations are set forth in detail in the treatise.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi was founded, it also followed Later Wei; the titles of the central offices differed somewhat from those south of the Yangzi, and the relevant regulations are set forth in detail in the treatise.

sentences.zh: 有周創據關右，日不暇給，洎乎克清江、漢，爰議憲章。

translations.literal: When Northern Zhou established itself in the Guanzhong region, it had no leisure even by day; only after pacifying the Jiang and Han regions did it turn to drafting statutes.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Zhou established itself in the Guanzhong region, it had scarcely a moment's rest; only after pacifying the Jiang and Han regions did it turn to drafting statutes.

sentences.zh: 酌禜鎬之遺文，置六官以綜務，詳其典制，有可稱焉。

translations.literal: Drawing on the surviving texts of the Zhou rites, it established the Six Offices to manage affairs; examining its institutions, there is much that deserves praise.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on the surviving texts of the Zhou rites, it established the Six Offices to manage affairs; examining its institutions, there is much that deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐極，百度伊始，複廢周官，還依漢、魏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Sui ascended the throne and the hundred institutions were just beginning, he again abolished the Zhou offices and returned to the Han and Wei pattern.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu of Sui ascended the throne and the hundred institutions were just beginning, he again abolished the Zhou offices and returned to the Han and Wei pattern.

sentences.zh: 唯以中書為內史，侍中為納言，自餘庶僚，頗有損益。

translations.literal: Only the Secretariat was renamed the Inner Secretariat, and the Attendant-in-Ordinary was renamed Chief Counselor; among the remaining officials there were considerable additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Secretariat was renamed the Inner Secretariat, and the Attendant-in-Ordinary was renamed Chief Counselor; among the remaining officials there were considerable additions and reductions.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，意存稽古，建官分職，率由舊章。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, his intent was to examine antiquity; in establishing offices and dividing duties, he generally followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, his intent was to examine antiquity; in establishing offices and dividing duties, he generally followed the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，始行新令。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, the new ordinances were first put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye, the new ordinances were first put into effect.

sentences.zh: 于時三川定鼎，萬國朝宗，衣冠文物，足為壯觀。

translations.literal: At that time the three rivers were settled and the tripod cast, the myriad states paid court homage, and the rites, robes, and cultural artifacts were truly magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the capital was firmly established, the myriad states paid court homage, and the rites, robes, and cultural artifacts were truly magnificent.

sentences.zh: 即而以人從欲，待下若仇，號令日改，官名月易。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he indulged the people's desires, treated subordinates like enemies, changed orders daily, and altered office titles monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he indulged every desire, treated subordinates like enemies, changed orders daily, and altered office titles monthly.

sentences.zh: 尋而南征不復，朝廷播遷，圖籍注記，多從散逸。

translations.literal: Before long the southern campaign did not return, the court was driven into exile, and many records, registers, and annotations were scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the southern campaign did not return, the court was driven into exile, and many records, registers, and annotations were scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 今之存錄者，不能詳備焉。

translations.literal: What survives in the present record cannot be complete in every detail.
translations.idiomatic: What survives in the present record cannot be complete in every detail.

sentences.zh: 梁武受命之初，官班多同宋、齊之舊，有丞相、太宰、太傅、太保、大將軍、大司馬、太尉、司徒、司空、開府儀同三司等官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wu of Liang's reign, the official ranks largely followed the old pattern of Song and Qi. There were the offices of Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand General, Grand Marshal, Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, Minister of Works, and Opener of an Office with Equal Privilege to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wu of Liang's reign, the official ranks largely followed the old pattern of Song and Qi. There were the offices of Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand General, Grand Marshal, Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, Minister of Works, and Opener of an Office with Equal Privilege to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 諸公及位從公開府者，置官屬。

translations.literal: For all dukes and those of rank equal to dukes who opened offices, staff officials were established.
translations.idiomatic: For all dukes and those of rank equal to dukes who opened offices, staff officials were established.

sentences.zh: 有長史、司馬、諮議參軍，掾屬從事中郎、記室、主簿、列曹參軍、行參軍、舍人等官。

translations.literal: There were the offices of Chief Administrator, Major, Advisory Aide, Staff Secretary, Attendant Secretary, Recorder, Chief Clerk, Department Aides, Acting Aide, and Attendant, among others.
translations.idiomatic: There were the offices of Chief Administrator, Major, Advisory Aide, Staff Secretary, Attendant Secretary, Recorder, Chief Clerk, Department Aides, Acting Aide, and Attendant, among others.

sentences.zh: 其司徒則有左、右二長史，又增置左西掾一人，自餘僚佐，同於二府。

translations.literal: The Minister over the Masses had left and right Chief Administrators; one additional Left Western Secretary was also established. The remaining staff followed the two offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister over the Masses had left and right Chief Administrators; one additional Left Western Secretary was also established. The remaining staff followed the two offices.

sentences.zh: 有公則置，無則省。

translations.literal: When there was a duke, they were established; when there was none, they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When there was a duke, they were established; when there was none, they were abolished.

sentences.zh: 而司徒無公，唯省舍人，余官常置。

translations.literal: When there was no duke as Minister over the Masses, only the Attendants were abolished; the remaining offices were regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: When there was no duke as Minister over the Masses, only the Attendants were abolished; the remaining offices were regularly established.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司，位次三公，諸將軍、左右光祿大夫，優者則加之，同三公，置官屬。

translations.literal: Opener of an Office with Equal Privilege to the Three Excellencies ranked next after the Three Excellencies. For generals and Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness, the superior were given this title; equal to the Three Excellencies, they established staff officials.
translations.idiomatic: Opener of an Office with Equal Privilege to the Three Excellencies ranked next after the Three Excellencies. Superior generals and Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness were given this title; equal to the Three Excellencies, they established staff officials.

sentences.zh: 特進，舊位從公。

translations.literal: Special Advancement: formerly its rank followed that of a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Special Advancement: formerly its rank followed that of a duke.

sentences.zh: 武帝以鄧禹列侯就第，特進奉朝請，是特引見之稱，無官定體。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu saw that Deng Yu, as a enfeoffed marquis living in retirement, held the title Special Advancement with Court Attendance, he recognized that this was merely a title for special audience and had no fixed institutional form.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu saw that Deng Yu, as an enfeoffed marquis living in retirement, held the title Special Advancement with Court Attendance, he recognized that this was merely a title for special audience and had no fixed institutional form.

sentences.zh: 於是革之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reformed it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he reformed it.

sentences.zh: 尚書省，置令，左、右僕射各一人。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs had one Director and one Left and one Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs had one Director and one Left and one Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 又置吏部、祠部、度支、左戶、都官、五兵等六尚書。

translations.literal: There were also six Ministers of the Department: Personnel, Rites, Revenue, Left Households, Justice, and Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: There were also six Ministers of the Department: Personnel, Rites, Revenue, Left Households, Justice, and Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 左右丞各一人。

translations.literal: There was one Left and one Right Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Left and one Right Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 吏部、刪定、三公、比部、祠部、儀曹、虞曹、主客、度支、殿中、金部、倉部、左戶、駕部、起部、屯田、都官、水部、庫部、功論、中兵、外兵、騎兵等郎二十三人。

translations.literal: There were twenty-three Directors: Personnel, Review and Fixation, Three Excellencies, Comparison, Rites, Ceremonial, Parks, Foreign Guests, Revenue, Palace Affairs, Gold, Granaries, Left Households, Chariots, Construction, Garrison Fields, Justice, Waterways, Armories, Merit Evaluation, Central Military, External Military, and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-three Directors: Personnel, Review and Fixation, Three Excellencies, Comparison, Rites, Ceremonial, Parks, Foreign Guests, Revenue, Palace Affairs, Gold, Granaries, Left Households, Chariots, Construction, Garrison Fields, Justice, Waterways, Armories, Merit Evaluation, Central Military, External Military, and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 令史百二十人，書令史百三十人。

translations.literal: There were 120 Clerks and 130 Writing Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: There were 120 Clerks and 130 Writing Clerks.

sentences.zh: 尚書掌出納王命，敷奏萬機。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs managed the receipt and dispatch of royal commands and the presentation of the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs managed the receipt and dispatch of royal commands and the presentation of the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 令總統之。

translations.literal: The Director presided over all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Director presided over all of it.

sentences.zh: 僕射副令，又與尚書分領諸曹。

translations.literal: The Vice Directors assisted the Director and also shared with the Ministers in overseeing the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Directors assisted the Director and also shared with the Ministers in overseeing the various bureaus.

sentences.zh: 令闕，則左僕射為主。

translations.literal: When the Director's post was vacant, the Left Vice Director took charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Director's post was vacant, the Left Vice Director took charge.

sentences.zh: 其祠部尚書多不置，以右僕射主之。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites was often not established; the Right Vice Director presided over that office.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites was often not established; the Right Vice Director presided over that office.

sentences.zh: 若左、右僕射並闕，則置尚書僕射以掌左事，置祠部尚書以掌右事。

translations.literal: If both Left and Right Vice Directors were vacant, a Vice Director of the Department was established to manage left affairs, and a Minister of Rites was established to manage right affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If both Left and Right Vice Directors were vacant, a Vice Director of the Department was established to manage left affairs, and a Minister of Rites was established to manage right affairs.

sentences.zh: 然則尚書僕射、祠部尚書不恆置矣。

translations.literal: Thus the Vice Director of the Department and the Minister of Rites were not permanently established.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Vice Director of the Department and the Minister of Rites were not permanently established.

sentences.zh: 又有起部尚書，營宗廟宮室則權置之。

translations.literal: There was also a Minister of Construction, established provisionally when ancestral temples or palaces were being built.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Minister of Construction, established provisionally when ancestral temples or palaces were being built.

sentences.zh: 事畢則省，以其事分屬都官、左戶二尚書。

translations.literal: When the work was finished it was abolished, and its duties were divided between the Ministers of Justice and Left Households.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished it was abolished, and its duties were divided between the Ministers of Justice and Left Households.

sentences.zh: 左、右丞各一人，佐令、僕射知省事。

translations.literal: There was one Left and one Right Assistant Director to assist the Director and Vice Directors in managing departmental affairs.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Left and one Right Assistant Director to assist the Director and Vice Directors in managing departmental affairs.

sentences.zh: 左掌台內分職儀、禁令、報人章，督錄近道文書章表奏事，糾諸不法。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant Director managed internal division of duties, protocol, prohibitions, seals for reporting personnel, supervised and recorded near-route documents, memorials, and reports, and corrected all irregularities.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant Director managed internal division of duties, protocol, prohibitions, seals for reporting personnel, supervised and recorded near-route documents, memorials, and reports, and corrected all irregularities.

sentences.zh: 右掌台內藏及廬舍、凡諸器用之物，督錄遠道文書章表奏事。

translations.literal: The Right Assistant Director managed the department's internal stores, quarters, and all utensils and goods, and supervised and recorded distant-route documents, memorials, and reports.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Assistant Director managed the department's internal stores, quarters, and all utensils and goods, and supervised and recorded distant-route documents, memorials, and reports.

sentences.zh: 凡諸尚書文書，詣中書省者，密事皆以挈囊盛之，封以左丞印。

translations.literal: For all documents of the Department of State Affairs sent to the Secretariat, confidential matters were placed in leather pouches and sealed with the Left Assistant Director's seal.
translations.idiomatic: For all documents of the Department of State Affairs sent to the Secretariat, confidential matters were placed in leather pouches and sealed with the Left Assistant Director's seal.

sentences.zh: 自晉以後，八座及郎中多不奏事。

translations.literal: From Jin onward, the Eight Seats and Directors often did not present memorials.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin onward, the Eight Seats and Directors often did not present memorials.

sentences.zh: 天監元年詔曰：「自禮闈陵替，曆茲永久，郎署備員，無取職事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian an edict said: "Since the ritual offices declined, a long time has passed; the Director's offices exist only to fill posts and have no real duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian an edict said: "Since the ritual offices declined, a long time has passed; the Director's offices exist only to fill posts and have no real duties.

sentences.zh: 糠粃文案，貴尚虛閑，空有趨墀之名，了無握蘭之實。

translations.literal: Chaff-filled paperwork is prized for idle leisure; they have the name of rushing to the court hall but none of the reality of holding the orchid seal.
translations.idiomatic: Their work is chaff-filled paperwork prized for idle leisure; they have the name of rushing to the court hall but none of the reality of holding the orchid seal.

sentences.zh: 曹郎可依昔奏事。

translations.literal: Department Directors may present memorials as in former times.
translations.idiomatic: Department Directors may present memorials as in former times.

sentences.zh: 」自是始奏事矣。

translations.literal: " From this time memorial presentation began again.
translations.idiomatic: From this time memorial presentation began again.

sentences.zh: 三年，置侍郎，視通直郎。

translations.literal: In the third year, Vice Directors were established, equal in rank to Direct Regular Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Vice Directors were established, equal in rank to Direct Regular Attendants.

sentences.zh: 其郎中在職勤能，滿二歲者，轉之。

translations.literal: Directors who served diligently and capably for two full years were transferred to these posts.
translations.idiomatic: Directors who served diligently and capably for two full years were transferred to these posts.

sentences.zh: 又有五都令史，與左、右丞共知所司。

translations.literal: There were also five Capital Clerks who, together with the Left and Right Assistant Directors, managed their respective departments.
translations.idiomatic: There were also five Capital Clerks who, together with the Left and Right Assistant Directors, managed their respective departments.

sentences.zh: 舊用人常輕，九年詔曰：「尚書五都，職參政要，非但總領眾局，亦乃方軌二丞。

translations.literal: Formerly those appointed to these posts were often held in low esteem. In the ninth year an edict said: "The five Capital Clerks of the Department of State Affairs participate in important government affairs; they not only oversee all bureaus but also stand on equal footing with the two Assistant Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly those appointed to these posts were often held in low esteem. In the ninth year an edict said: "The five Capital Clerks of the Department of State Affairs participate in important government affairs; they not only oversee all bureaus but also stand on equal footing with the two Assistant Directors.

sentences.zh: 頃雖求才，未臻妙簡，可革用士流，每盡時彥，庶同持領，秉此群目。

translations.literal: Recently, though talent has been sought, the finest selections have not yet been achieved. They should be drawn from the scholar-official class, always selecting the outstanding men of the age, so that they may jointly hold the reins and oversee these many offices.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, though talent has been sought, the finest selections have not yet been achieved. They should be drawn from the scholar-official class, always selecting the outstanding men of the age, so that they may jointly hold the reins and oversee these many offices.

sentences.zh: 」於是以都令史視奉朝請。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Capital Clerks were treated as equal to Court Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Capital Clerks were treated as equal to Court Attendants.

sentences.zh: 其年，以太學博士劉納兼殿中都，司空法曹參軍劉顯兼吏部都，太學博士孔虔孫兼金部都，司空法曹參軍蕭軌兼左戶都，宣毅墨曹參軍王顒兼中兵都。

translations.literal: That year, the Imperial Academy Erudite Liu Na was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Palace Affairs; Liu Xian, Legal Bureau Aide of the Minister of Works, was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Personnel; Kong Qiansun, Imperial Academy Erudite, was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Gold; Xiao Gui, Legal Bureau Aide of the Minister of Works, was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Left Households; and Wang Yong, Ink Bureau Aide of the Propagation of Martial Virtue, was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Central Military.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the Imperial Academy Erudite Liu Na was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Palace Affairs; Liu Xian, Legal Bureau Aide of the Minister of Works, was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Personnel; Kong Qiansun, Imperial Academy Erudite, was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Gold; Xiao Gui, Legal Bureau Aide of the Minister of Works, was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Left Households; and Wang Yong, Ink Bureau Aide of the Propagation of Martial Virtue, was additionally appointed Capital Clerk of Central Military.

sentences.zh: 五人並以才地兼美，首膺茲選矣。

translations.literal: All five were men of combined talent and standing, and were the first to receive this selection.
translations.idiomatic: All five were men of combined talent and standing, and were the first to receive this selection.

sentences.zh: 駕部又別領車府署，庫部領南、北武庫二署令丞。

translations.literal: The Chariots Department also separately oversaw the Chariot Office; the Armories Department oversaw the Directors of the Southern and Northern Military Storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: The Chariots Department also separately oversaw the Charrion Office; the Armories Department oversaw the Directors of the Southern and Northern Military Storehouses.

sentences.zh: 門下省置侍中、給事黃門侍郎各四人，掌侍從左右，擯相威儀，盡規獻納，糾正違闕。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretariat had four Attendants-in-Ordinary and four Gentlemen Attendants of the Yellow Gate, who attended at the ruler's side, arranged ceremonial dignity, offered remonstrance and advice, and corrected violations and omissions.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Secretariat had four Attendants-in-Ordinary and four Gentlemen Attendants of the Yellow Gate, who attended at the ruler's side, arranged ceremonial dignity, offered remonstrance and advice, and corrected violations and omissions.

sentences.zh: 監令嘗禦藥，封璽書。

translations.literal: They supervised the imperial medicines and sealed the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised the imperial medicines and sealed the edicts.

sentences.zh: 侍中高功者，在職一年，詔加侍中祭酒，與侍郎高功者一人，對掌禁令，公車、太官、太醫等令，驊騮廄丞。

translations.literal: For Attendants-in-Ordinary of high merit, after one year in office an edict added the title Attendant-in-Ordinary Libationer; together with one highly meritorious Gentleman Attendant, they jointly managed prohibitions, the Directors of the Public Chariots, Grand Provisioner, Imperial Physician, and the Director of the Hualiu Stable.
translations.idiomatic: For Attendants-in-Ordinary of high merit, after one year in office an edict added the title Attendant-in-Ordinary Libationer; together with one highly meritorious Gentleman Attendant, they jointly managed prohibitions, the Directors of the Public Chariots, Grand Provisioner, Imperial Physician, and the Director of the Hualiu Stable.

sentences.zh: 集書省置散騎常侍、通直散騎常侍各四人。

translations.literal: The Secretariat for Drafting had four Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue and four Direct Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat for Drafting had four Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue and four Direct Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎常侍無員。

translations.literal: Extra Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Extra Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎、通直郎各四人。

translations.literal: There were four Gentlemen of the Loose Retinue and four Direct Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Gentlemen of the Loose Retinue and four Direct Attendants.

sentences.zh: 又有員外散騎侍郎、給事中、奉朝請、常侍侍郎，掌侍從左右，獻納得失，省諸奏聞文書。

translations.literal: There were also Extra Gentlemen of the Loose Retinue, Gentlemen for Attending to Affairs, Court Attendants, and Regular Attendant Gentlemen, who attended at the ruler's side, offered advice on gains and losses, and reviewed all memorials submitted for the ruler's attention.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Extra Gentlemen of the Loose Retinue, Gentlemen for Attending to Affairs, Court Attendants, and Regular Attendant Gentlemen, who attended at the ruler's side, offered advice on gains and losses, and reviewed all memorials submitted for the ruler's attention.

sentences.zh: 意異者，隨事為駁。

translations.literal: Where they found disagreement, they rebutted the matter as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Where they found disagreement, they rebutted the matter as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 集錄比詔比璽，為諸優文策文，平處諸文章詩頌。

translations.literal: They collected and recorded edicts and seal-proclamations, drafted laudatory documents and policy essays, and edited essays, poems, and eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: They collected and recorded edicts and seal-proclamations, drafted laudatory documents and policy essays, and edited essays, poems, and eulogies.

sentences.zh: 常侍高功者一人為祭酒，與侍郎高功者一人，對掌禁令，糾諸逋違。

translations.literal: One highly meritorious Regular Attendant served as Libationer; together with one highly meritorious Gentleman Attendant, they jointly managed prohibitions and corrected all delinquencies.
translations.idiomatic: One highly meritorious Regular Attendant served as Libationer; together with one highly meritorious Gentleman Attendant, they jointly managed prohibitions and corrected all delinquencies.

sentences.zh: 駙馬、奉車、車騎三都尉，並無員。

translations.literal: The Commandants of the Imperial Son-in-Law, Chariot Service, and Chariots and Cavalry had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandants of the Imperial Son-in-Law, Chariot Service, and Chariots and Cavalry had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 駙馬以加尚公主者，無班秩。

translations.literal: Imperial Son-in-Law was conferred on those who married imperial princesses and carried no formal rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Son-in-Law was conferred on those who married imperial princesses and carried no formal rank.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、通直散騎常侍、員外散騎常侍，舊並為顯職，與侍中通官。

translations.literal: Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue, Direct Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue, and Extra Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue were formerly all eminent offices and shared office with Attendants-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue, Direct Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue, and Extra Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue were formerly all eminent offices and shared office with Attendants-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 宋代以來，或輕或雜，其官漸替。

translations.literal: From the Song period onward they were sometimes devalued or mixed with other duties, and the office gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song period onward they were sometimes devalued or mixed with other duties, and the office gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 天監六年革選，詔曰：「在昔晉初，仰惟盛化，常侍、侍中，並奏帷幄，員外常侍，特為清顯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjian, when the selection system was reformed, an edict said: "In former times at the beginning of Jin, reflecting on that flourishing age, Regular Attendants and Attendants-in-Ordinary both presented memorials within the inner curtain; Extra Regular Attendants were especially clear and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjian, when the selection system was reformed, an edict said: "In former times at the beginning of Jin, reflecting on that flourishing age, Regular Attendants and Attendants-in-Ordinary both presented memorials within the inner curtain; Extra Regular Attendants were especially clear and eminent.

sentences.zh: 陸始名公之胤，位居納言，曲蒙優禮，方有斯授。

translations.literal: Lu Kai, descendant of a famous house, held the position of Chief Counselor and received special favor before this appointment was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai, descendant of a famous house, held the position of Chief Counselor and received special favor before this appointment was granted.

sentences.zh: 可分門下二局，委散騎常侍尚書案奏，分曹入集書。

translations.literal: The two bureaus of the Palace Secretariat may be divided, entrusting Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue with Department memorials, each bureau entering the Secretariat for Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: The two bureaus of the Palace Secretariat may be divided, entrusting Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue with Department memorials, each bureau entering the Secretariat for Drafting.

sentences.zh: 通直常侍，本為顯爵，員外之選，宜參舊准人數，依正員格。

translations.literal: Direct Regular Attendant was originally an eminent rank; selections for Extra posts should follow the old quota of numbers according to the regular establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Regular Attendant was originally an eminent rank; selections for Extra posts should follow the old quota of numbers according to the regular establishment.

sentences.zh: 」自是散騎視侍中，通直視中丞，員外視黃門郎。

translations.literal: " From this time Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue were treated as equal to Attendants-in-Ordinary, Direct Regular Attendants as equal to Censor-in-Chief, and Extra Attendants as equal to Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: From this time Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue were treated as equal to Attendants-in-Ordinary, Direct Regular Attendants as equal to Censor-in-Chief, and Extra Attendants as equal to Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 中書省置監、令各一人，掌出內帝命。

translations.literal: The Secretariat had one Supervisor and one Director, who managed the issuance of the emperor's commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat had one Supervisor and one Director, who managed the issuance of the emperor's commands.

sentences.zh: 侍郎四人，功高者一人，主省內事。

translations.literal: There were four Vice Directors; the one of highest merit managed internal affairs of the department.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Vice Directors; the one of highest merit managed internal affairs of the department.

sentences.zh: 又有通事舍人、主事令史等員，及置令史，以承其事。

translations.literal: There were also Attendants for General Affairs, Chief Clerks, and other posts, as well as Clerks established to carry out the work.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Attendants for General Affairs, Chief Clerks, and other posts, as well as Clerks established to carry out the work.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人，舊入直閤內。

translations.literal: Attendants for General Affairs formerly entered duty within the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants for General Affairs formerly entered duty within the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 梁用人殊重，簡以才能，不限資地，多以他官兼領。

translations.literal: Liang held this appointment in special esteem, selecting by ability without limiting family background; many held it concurrently with other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liang held this appointment in special esteem, selecting by ability without limiting family background; many held it concurrently with other offices.

sentences.zh: 其後除通事，直曰中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later the title Attendant for General Affairs was abolished and they were directly called Secretaries of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later the title Attendant for General Affairs was abolished and they were directly called Secretaries of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秘書省置監、丞各一人，郎四人，掌國之典籍圖書。

translations.literal: The Imperial Library had one Supervisor and one Assistant Director, four Directors, who managed the state's classics and books.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Library had one Supervisor and one Assistant Director and four Directors, who managed the state's classics and books.

sentences.zh: 著作郎一人，佐郎八人，掌國史，集注起居。

translations.literal: There was one Master of Writing and eight Assistant Directors, who managed the national history and collected and annotated the records of daily attendance.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Master of Writing and eight Assistant Directors, who managed the national history and collected and annotated the records of daily attendance.

sentences.zh: 著作郎謂之大著作，梁初周舍、裴子野，皆以他官領之。

translations.literal: The Master of Writing was called the Grand Master of Writing; in the early Liang, Zhou She and Pei Ziye both held it concurrently with other offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Writing was called the Grand Master of Writing; in the early Liang, Zhou She and Pei Ziye both held it concurrently with other offices.

sentences.zh: 又有撰史學士，亦知史書。

translations.literal: There were also Scholar-Historians for Compilation, who also managed historical records.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Scholar-Historians for Compilation, who also managed historical records.

sentences.zh: 佐郎為起家之選。

translations.literal: Assistant Director was the entry-level selection for office.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director was the entry-level selection for office.

sentences.zh: 謁者台，僕射一人，掌朝覲賓饗之事。

translations.literal: The Herald Office had one Vice Director, who managed affairs of court audience and guest banquets.
translations.idiomatic: The Herald Office had one Vice Director, who managed affairs of court audience and guest banquets.

sentences.zh: 屬官謁者十人，掌奉詔出使拜假，朝會擯贊。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials included ten Heralds, who managed missions bearing edicts, leave requests, and arrangement and praise at court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officials included ten Heralds, who managed missions bearing edicts, leave requests, and arrangement and praise at court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 高功者一人為假史，掌差次謁者。

translations.literal: The one of highest merit served as Acting Clerk and managed the assignment of Heralds.
translations.idiomatic: The one of highest merit served as Acting Clerk and managed the assignment of Heralds.

sentences.zh: 諸卿，梁初猶依宋、齊，皆無卿名。

translations.literal: The various ministers: in the early Liang they still followed Song and Qi and had no ministerial titles.
translations.idiomatic: The various ministers: in the early Liang they still followed Song and Qi and had no ministerial titles.

sentences.zh: 天監七年，乙太常為太常卿，加置宗正卿，以大司農為司農卿，三卿是為春卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianjian, the Grand Master of Ceremonies was renamed Minister of Ceremonies; the Minister of the Imperial Clan was also established—these three ministers were the Spring Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianjian, the Grand Master of Ceremonies was renamed Minister of Ceremonies; the Minister of the Imperial Clan was also established—these three ministers were the Spring Ministers.

sentences.zh: 加置太府卿，以少府為少府卿，加置太僕卿，三卿是為夏卿。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Grand Granary was established; the Minister of the Palace Stores was renamed Minister of the Palace Stores; the Minister of the Imperial Stud was also established—these three were the Summer Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Grand Granary was established; the Minister of the Palace Stores was renamed Minister of the Palace Stores; the Minister of the Imperial Stud was also established—these three were the Summer Ministers.

sentences.zh: 以衛尉為衛尉卿，廷尉為廷尉卿，將作大匠為大匠卿。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Guards was renamed Commandant of the Guards; the Commandant of Punishments was renamed Commandant of Punishments; the Master of Construction was renamed Master of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Guards was renamed Commandant of the Guards; the Commandant of Punishments was renamed Commandant of Punishments; the Master of Construction was renamed Master of Construction.

sentences.zh: 三卿是為秋卿。

translations.literal: These three were the Autumn Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: These three were the Autumn Ministers.

sentences.zh: 以光祿勳為光祿卿，大鴻臚為鴻臚卿，都水使者為太舟卿，三卿是為冬卿。

translations.literal: The Supervisor of the Masters of Brilliant Happiness was renamed Minister of Brilliant Happiness; the Grand Herald was renamed Minister of the Grand Herald; the Commissioner of Waterways was renamed Minister of Great Vessels—these three were the Winter Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervisor of the Masters of Brilliant Happiness was renamed Minister of Brilliant Happiness; the Grand Herald was renamed Minister of the Grand Herald; the Commissioner of Waterways was renamed Minister of Great Vessels—these three were the Winter Ministers.

sentences.zh: 凡十二卿，皆置丞及功曹、主簿。

translations.literal: In all there were twelve ministers; each had an Assistant Director, Merit Clerk, and Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were twelve ministers; each had an Assistant Director, Merit Clerk, and Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 而太常視金紫光祿大夫，統明堂、二廟、太史、太祝、廩犧、太樂、鼓吹、乘黃、北館、典客館等令丞，及陵監、國學等。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies was treated as equal to the Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord; he oversaw the Directors and Assistant Directors of the Bright Hall, Two Temples, Grand Astrologer, Grand Sacrificer, Stable Sacrifices, Grand Music, Drum and Pipe, Chariot Service, Northern Lodge, and Guest Reception Hall, as well as Tomb Supervisors and the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies was treated as equal to the Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord; he oversaw the Directors and Assistant Directors of the Bright Hall, Two Temples, Grand Astrologer, Grand Sacrificer, Stable Sacrifices, Grand Music, Drum and Pipe, Chariot Service, Northern Lodge, and Guest Reception Hall, as well as Tomb Supervisors and the National Academy.

sentences.zh: 又置協律校尉、總章校尉監、掌故、樂正之屬，以掌樂事。

translations.literal: Harmony Regulators, General Regulation Supervisors, Archivists, and Music Masters were also established to manage musical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony Regulators, General Regulation Supervisors, Archivists, and Music Masters were also established to manage musical affairs.

sentences.zh: 太樂又有清商署丞，太史別有靈台丞。

translations.literal: Grand Music also had an Assistant Director of the Clear Shang Office; the Grand Astrologer separately had an Assistant Director of the Spirit Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Music also had an Assistant Director of the Clear Shang Office; the Grand Astrologer separately had an Assistant Director of the Spirit Tower.

sentences.zh: 詔以為陵監之名，不出前誥，且宗廟憲章，既備典禮，園寢職司，理不容異，諸正陵先立監者改為令。

translations.literal: An edict held that the title Tomb Supervisor did not appear in earlier proclamations; since the regulations for ancestral temples were already complete in the canonical rites, the duties of managing imperial tombs could not be treated differently, and all Tomb Supervisors previously established at major tombs were changed to Directors.
translations.idiomatic: An edict held that the title Tomb Supervisor did not appear in earlier proclamations; since the regulations for ancestral temples were already complete in the canonical rites, the duties of managing imperial tombs could not be treated differently, and all Tomb Supervisors previously established at major tombs were changed to Directors.

sentences.zh: 於是陵置令矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Directors were established for the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Directors were established for the tombs.

sentences.zh: 國學，有祭酒一人，博士二人，助教十人，太學博士八人。

translations.literal: The National Academy had one Libationer, two Erudites, ten Assistant Instructors, and eight Erudites of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The National Academy had one Libationer, two Erudites, ten Assistant Instructors, and eight Erudites of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 又有限外博士員。

translations.literal: There were also Extra Erudites beyond the regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Extra Erudites beyond the regular quota.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，置五經博士各一人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian, one Erudite for each of the Five Classics was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianjian, one Erudite for each of the Five Classics was established.

sentences.zh: 舊國子學生，限以貴賤，帝欲招來後進，五館生皆引寒門俊才，不限人數。

translations.literal: Formerly students of the National Academy were limited by noble and base status; the emperor wished to recruit promising young men, and students of the Five Halls were all drawn from talented men of humble families without limit on numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly students of the National Academy were limited by noble and base status; the emperor wished to recruit promising young men, and students of the Five Halls were all drawn from talented men of humble families without limit on numbers.

sentences.zh: 大同七年，國子祭酒到溉等，又表立正言博士一人，位視國子博士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong, the National Academy Libationer Dao Gai and others also memorialized to establish one Erudite of Standard Speech, equal in rank to the National Academy Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Datong, the National Academy Libationer Dao Gai and others also memorialized to establish one Erudite of Standard Speech, equal in rank to the National Academy Erudite.

sentences.zh: 置助教二人。

translations.literal: Two Assistant Instructors were established.
translations.idiomatic: Two Assistant Instructors were established.

sentences.zh: 宗正卿，位視列曹尚書，主皇室外戚之籍。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Imperial Clan was treated as equal to a Minister of a Department; he managed the registers of the imperial clan and maternal relatives.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Imperial Clan was treated as equal to a Minister of a Department; he managed the registers of the imperial clan and maternal relatives.

sentences.zh: 以宗室為之。

translations.literal: A member of the imperial clan held the post.
translations.idiomatic: A member of the imperial clan held the post.

sentences.zh: 司農卿，位視散騎常侍，主農功倉廩。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Grand Granary was treated as equal to a Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue; he managed agricultural work and granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Grand Granary was treated as equal to a Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue; he managed agricultural work and granaries.

sentences.zh: 統太倉、導官、籍田、上林令，又管樂游、北苑丞，左右中部三倉丞，莢庫、荻庫、箬庫丞，湖西諸屯主。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Directors of the Grand Granary, Guiding Granary, Registered Fields, and Upper Forest, and also managed the Assistant Directors of the Music Park and Northern Park, the Assistant Directors of the Left, Right, and Central Three Granaries, and the Assistant Directors of the Bean Storehouse, Reed Storehouse, and Bamboo Storehouse, as well as the Chiefs of the various garrison fields west of the lake.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Directors of the Grand Granary, Guiding Granary, Registered Fields, and Upper Forest, and also managed the Assistant Directors of the Music Park and Northern Park, the Assistant Directors of the Left, Right, and Central Three Granaries, and the Assistant Directors of the Bean Storehouse, Reed Storehouse, and Bamboo Storehouse, as well as the Chiefs of the various garrison fields west of the lake.

sentences.zh: 天監九年，又置勸農謁者，視殿中禦史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianjian, Agricultural Encouragement Heralds were also established, treated as equal to Palace Censors.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianjian, Agricultural Encouragement Heralds were also established, treated as equal to Palace Censors.

sentences.zh: 太府卿，位視宗正，掌金帛府帑。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Palace Treasury was treated as equal to the Minister of the Imperial Clan; he managed gold, silk, and the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Palace Treasury was treated as equal to the Minister of the Imperial Clan; he managed gold, silk, and the treasury stores.

sentences.zh: 統左右藏令、上庫丞，掌太倉、南北市令。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Directors of the Left and Right Storehouses and the Assistant Director of the Upper Storehouse, and managed the Directors of the Grand Granary and the Southern and Northern Markets.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Directors of the Left and Right Storehouses and the Assistant Director of the Upper Storehouse, and managed the Directors of the Grand Granary and the Southern and Northern Markets.

sentences.zh: 關津亦皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Pass checkpoints and ferry stations also fell under his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Pass checkpoints and ferry stations also fell under his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 少府卿，位視尚書左丞，置材官將軍、左中右尚方、甄官、平水署、南塘邸稅庫、東西冶、中黃、細作、炭庫、紙官、柴署等令丞。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Palace Stores was treated as equal to the Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he established the General of Works Materials, the Left, Central, and Right Masters of Upper Works, the Master of the Foundry, the Office of Level Waterways, the Southern Pond Tax Storehouse, the Eastern and Western Smelting Works, the Central Yellow Office, Fine Craftsmanship, the Charcoal Storehouse, the Paper Office, and the Firewood Office, each with Directors and Assistant Directors.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Palace Stores was treated as equal to the Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he established the General of Works Materials, the Left, Central, and Right Masters of Upper Works, the Master of the Foundry, the Office of Level Waterways, the Southern Pond Tax Storehouse, the Eastern and Western Smelting Works, the Central Yellow Office, Fine Craftsmanship, the Charcoal Storehouse, the Paper Office, and the Firewood Office, each with Directors and Assistant Directors.

sentences.zh: 衛僕卿，位視黃門侍郎，統南馬牧、左右牧、龍廄、內外廄丞。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Imperial Stud was treated as equal to a Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate; he oversaw the Directors of the Southern Horse Pasture, Left and Right Pastures, Dragon Stable, and Inner and Outer Stables.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Imperial Stud was treated as equal to a Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate; he oversaw the Directors of the Southern Horse Pasture, Left and Right Pastures, Dragon Stable, and Inner and Outer Stables.

sentences.zh: 又有弘訓太僕，亦置屬官。

translations.literal: There was also the Propagation of Instruction Imperial Stud, which also had subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Propagation of Instruction Imperial Stud, which also had subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 衛尉卿，位視侍中，掌宮門屯兵。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Guards was treated as equal to an Attendant-in-Ordinary; he managed the garrison troops of the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Guards was treated as equal to an Attendant-in-Ordinary; he managed the garrison troops of the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 卿每月、丞每旬行宮徼，糾察不法。

translations.literal: The Minister inspected the palace monthly and the Assistant Director every ten days, correcting all irregularities.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister inspected the palace monthly and the Assistant Director every ten days, correcting all irregularities.

sentences.zh: 統武庫令、公車司馬令。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Director of the Military Storehouse and the Director of the Public Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Director of the Military Storehouse and the Director of the Public Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又有弘訓衛尉，亦置屬官。

translations.literal: There was also the Propagation of Instruction Commandant of the Guards, which also had subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Propagation of Instruction Commandant of the Guards, which also had subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 廷尉卿，梁國初建，曰大理，天監元年，複改為廷尉。

translations.literal: The Commandant of Punishments: when Liang was first established it was called the Court of Great Reason; in the first year of Tianjian it was again changed to Commandant of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Punishments: when Liang was first established it was called the Court of Great Reason; in the first year of Tianjian it was again changed to Commandant of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 有正、監、平三人。

translations.literal: There were three officials: Director, Supervisor, and Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: There were three officials: Director, Supervisor, and Assessor.

sentences.zh: 元會，廷尉三官與建康三官，皆法冠玄衣朝服，以監東、西、中華門。

translations.literal: At the New Year's assembly, the three officials of the Commandant of Punishments and the three officials of Jiankang all wore law caps and dark robes in court dress to supervise the Eastern, Western, and Central Chinese Gates.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year's assembly, the three officials of the Commandant of Punishments and the three officials of Jiankang all wore law caps and dark robes in court dress to supervise the Eastern, Western, and Central Chinese Gates.

sentences.zh: 手執方木，長三尺，方一寸，謂之執方。

translations.literal: They held in their hands a square piece of wood three feet long and one inch square, called the Holder of the Square.
translations.idiomatic: They held in their hands a square piece of wood three feet long and one inch square, called the Holder of the Square.

sentences.zh: 四年，置胄子律博士，位視員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an Erudite of Military Law for the Crown Prince was established, equal in rank to an Extra Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, an Erudite of Military Law for the Crown Prince was established, equal in rank to an Extra Director.

sentences.zh: 大匠卿，位視太僕，掌土木之工。

translations.literal: The Master of Construction was treated as equal to the Minister of the Imperial Stud; he managed earth and wood construction.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Construction was treated as equal to the Minister of the Imperial Stud; he managed earth and wood construction.

sentences.zh: 統左、右校諸署。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Left and Right School and various offices.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Left and Right School and various offices.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿，位視太子中庶子，掌宮殿門戶。

translations.literal: The Minister of Brilliant Happiness was treated as equal to the Crown Prince's Supervisor of the Household; he managed the palace gates and doorways.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Brilliant Happiness was treated as equal to the Crown Prince's Supervisor of the Household; he managed the palace gates and doorways.

sentences.zh: 統守宮、黃門、華林園、暴室等令。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Directors of the Palace Guard, Yellow Gate, Hualin Park, and Punishment Office.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Directors of the Palace Guard, Yellow Gate, Hualin Park, and Punishment Office.

sentences.zh: 又有左右光祿、金紫光祿、太中、中散等大夫，並無員，以養老疾。

translations.literal: There were also the Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness, Masters of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, Grand Masters of Palace Attendance, and Masters of Palace Attendance, all without fixed quota, to support the aged and infirm.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness, Masters of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, Grand Masters of Palace Attendance, and Masters of Palace Attendance, all without fixed quota, to support the aged and infirm.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚卿，位視尚書左丞，掌導護贊拜。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Grand Herald was treated as equal to the Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he managed guidance, protection, and ceremonial praise.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Grand Herald was treated as equal to the Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he managed guidance, protection, and ceremonial praise.

sentences.zh: 太舟卿，梁初為都水台，使者一人，參軍事二人，河堤謁者八人。

translations.literal: The Minister of Great Vessels: in the early Liang it was the Waterways Office, with one Commissioner, two Aides, and eight Waterway Heralds.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Great Vessels: in the early Liang it was the Waterways Office, with one Commissioner, two Aides, and eight Waterway Heralds.

sentences.zh: 七年，改焉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year it was changed.

sentences.zh: 位視中書郎，列卿之最末者也。

translations.literal: Its rank was treated as equal to a Secretary of the Secretariat; it was the lowest among the ranked ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Its rank was treated as equal to a Secretary of the Secretariat; it was the lowest among the ranked ministers.

sentences.zh: 主舟航堤渠。

translations.literal: It managed boats, navigation, dikes, and canals.
translations.idiomatic: It managed boats, navigation, dikes, and canals.

sentences.zh: 大長秋，主諸宦者，以司宮闈之職。

translations.literal: The Grand Director of the Palace Domain managed all eunuchs and oversaw the duties of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Director of the Palace Domain managed all eunuchs and oversaw the duties of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 統黃門、中署、奚官、暴室、華林等署。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Yellow Gate, Central Office, Palace Women, Punishment Office, and Hualin offices.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Yellow Gate, Central Office, Palace Women, Punishment Office, and Hualin offices.

sentences.zh: 領軍，護軍，左、右衛、驍騎、遊騎等六將軍，是為六軍，又有中領、中護，資輕於領、護。

translations.literal: The Commander-in-Chief, Protector-General, Left and Right Guard, Valiant Cavalry, and Mobile Cavalry Generals—these were the Six Armies; there were also Central Commander-in-Chief and Central Protector-General, whose qualifications were lower than those of the Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: The Commander-in-Chief, Protector-General, Left and Right Guard, Valiant Cavalry, and Mobile Cavalry Generals—these were the Six Armies; there were also Central Commander-in-Chief and Central Protector-General, whose qualifications were lower than those of the Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 又左右前後四將軍，左右中郎將，屯騎、步騎、越騎、長水、射聲等五營校尉，武賁、冗從、羽林三將軍，積射、強弩二軍，殿中將軍、武騎之職，皆以分司丹禁，侍衛左右。

translations.literal: There were also the Front, Left, Right, and Rear Four Generals, Left and Right Commandants of the Central Guard, the Five Camp Commandants of Garrison Cavalry, Foot Cavalry, Yue Cavalry, Long River, and Shooter Sound, the Three Generals of the Martial Tiger, Attendant Retinue, and Forest of Feathers, the Two Armies of Accumulated Shooter and Strong Crossbow, and the Palace Generals and Martial Cavalry—all dividing duties within the vermilion forbidden zone to attend and guard at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Front, Left, Right, and Rear Four Generals, Left and Right Commandants of the Central Guard, the Five Camp Commandants of Garrison Cavalry, Foot Cavalry, Yue Cavalry, Long River, and Shooter Sound, the Three Generals of the Martial Tiger, Attendant Retinue, and Forest of Feathers, the Two Armies of Accumulated Shooter and Strong Crossbow, and the Palace Generals and Martial Cavalry—all dividing duties within the vermilion forbidden zone to attend and guard at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 天監六年，置左右驍騎、左右遊擊將軍，位視二率。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjian, Left and Right Valiant Cavalry and Left and Right Mobile Attack Generals were established, equal in rank to the Two Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjian, Left and Right Valiant Cavalry and Left and Right Mobile Attack Generals were established, equal in rank to the Two Commanders.

sentences.zh: 改舊驍騎曰雲騎，遊擊曰遊騎，降左右驍、遊一階。

translations.literal: The old Valiant Cavalry was renamed Cloud Cavalry and Mobile Attack was renamed Mobile Cavalry; Left and Right Valiant and Mobile were lowered one step.
translations.idiomatic: The old Valiant Cavalry was renamed Cloud Cavalry and Mobile Attack was renamed Mobile Cavalry; Left and Right Valiant and Mobile were lowered one step.

sentences.zh: 又置硃衣直閣將軍，以經為方牧者為之。

translations.literal: Scarlet-Robed Direct Gate Generals were also established, filled by those who had served as regional governors.
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet-Robed Direct Gate Generals were also established, filled by those who had served as regional governors.

sentences.zh: 其以左右驍、遊帶領者，量給儀從。

translations.literal: For those who held Left and Right Valiant and Mobile concurrently, ceremonial attendants were granted according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: For those who held Left and Right Valiant and Mobile concurrently, ceremonial attendants were granted according to measure.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅一人，位視尚書令。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor: one person, rank equal to the Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor: one person, rank equal to the Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 少傅一人，位視左僕射。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor: one person, rank equal to the Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor: one person, rank equal to the Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 天監初，又置東宮常侍，皆散騎常侍為之。

translations.literal: In the early Tianjian period, Eastern Palace Regular Attendants were also established, all filled by Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianjian period, Eastern Palace Regular Attendants were also established, all filled by Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue.

sentences.zh: 詹事，位視中護軍，任總宮朝。

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Crown Prince's Household: rank equal to the Central Protector-General; he had overall charge of the palace court.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendent of the Crown Prince's Household: rank equal to the Central Protector-General; he had overall charge of the palace court.

sentences.zh: 二傅及詹事，各置丞、功曹、主簿。

translations.literal: The Two Tutors and the Superintendent each had an Assistant Director, Merit Clerk, and Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Tutors and the Superintendent each had an Assistant Director, Merit Clerk, and Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 五官、家令、率更令僕各一人。

translations.literal: Five Officers, Director of the Household, and Commandant of the Watch and Gate: one each.
translations.idiomatic: Five Officers, Director of the Household, and Commandant of the Watch and Gate: one each.

sentences.zh: 家令，自宋、齊已來，清流者不為之。

translations.literal: Director of the Household: from Song and Qi onward, men of pure lineage did not hold this post.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Household: from Song and Qi onward, men of pure lineage did not hold this post.

sentences.zh: 天監六年，帝以三卿陵替，乃詔革選。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjian, because the three ministers had declined, the emperor ordered a reform of selections.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjian, because the three ministers had declined, the emperor ordered a reform of selections.

sentences.zh: 家令視通直常侍，率更、僕視黃門三等，皆置丞。

translations.literal: Director of the Household was treated as equal to Direct Regular Attendant; Commandant of the Watch and Gate and Steward were treated as equal to the third rank of Yellow Gate; all had Assistant Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Household was treated as equal to Direct Regular Attendant; Commandant of the Watch and Gate and Steward were treated as equal to the third rank of Yellow Gate; all had Assistant Directors.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，以昭明太子妃居金華宮，又置金華家令。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, because the Crown Prince Zhao Ming's consort resided at Jinhua Palace, a Jinhua Director of the Household was also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong, because the Crown Prince Zhao Ming's consort resided at Jinhua Palace, a Jinhua Director of the Household was also established.

sentences.zh: 左、右衛率各一人，位視禦史中丞。

translations.literal: Left and Right Commandants of the Guard: one each, rank equal to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Commandants of the Guard: one each, rank equal to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 各有丞。

translations.literal: Each had an Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: Each had an Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 左率領果毅、統遠、立忠、建寧、陵鋒、夷寇、祚德等七營，右率領崇榮、永吉、崇和、細射等四營。

translations.literal: The Left Commander led the seven camps of Guoyi, Tongyuan, Lizhong, Jianning, Lingfeng, Yikou, and Zoude; the Right Commander led the four camps of Chongrong, Yongji, Chonghe, and Xishe.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Commander led the seven camps of Guoyi, Tongyuan, Lizhong, Jianning, Lingfeng, Yikou, and Zoude; the Right Commander led the four camps of Chongrong, Yongji, Chonghe, and Xishe.

sentences.zh: 二率各置殿中將軍十人，員外將軍十人，正員司馬四人。

translations.literal: Each of the Two Commanders established ten Palace Generals, ten Extra Generals, and four regular Majors.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the Two Commanders established ten Palace Generals, ten Extra Generals, and four regular Majors.

sentences.zh: 又有員外司馬督官。

translations.literal: There were also Extra Majors supervising officials.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Extra Majors supervising officials.

sentences.zh: 共屯騎、步兵、翊軍三校尉各一人，謂之三校。

translations.literal: Together the Commandants of Garrison Cavalry, Foot Cavalry, and Support Army: one each—these were called the Three Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Together the Commandants of Garrison Cavalry, Foot Cavalry, and Support Army: one each—these were called the Three Commandants.

sentences.zh: 旅賁中郎將、冗從僕射各一人，謂之二將。

translations.literal: Central Commandant of the Imperial Guard and Vice Director of the Attendant Retinue: one each—these were called the Two Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Central Commandant of the Imperial Guard and Vice Director of the Attendant Retinue: one each—these were called the Two Generals.

sentences.zh: 左、右積弩將軍各一人。

translations.literal: Left and Right Accumulated Crossbow Generals: one each.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Accumulated Crossbow Generals: one each.

sentences.zh: 門大夫一人，視謁者僕射。

translations.literal: Gate Grand Master: one person, treated as equal to Vice Director of Heralds.
translations.idiomatic: Gate Grand Master: one person, treated as equal to Vice Director of Heralds.

sentences.zh: 中庶子四人，功高者一人為祭酒。

translations.literal: Supervisors of the Household: four persons; the one of highest merit served as Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors of the Household: four persons; the one of highest merit served as Libationer.

sentences.zh: 行則負璽，前後部護駕。

translations.literal: When traveling he carried the seal; he escorted the ruler before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: When traveling he carried the seal; he escorted the ruler before and behind.

sentences.zh: 中舍人四人，功高者一人，與中庶子祭酒共掌其坊之禁令。

translations.literal: Attendants of the Household: four persons; the one of highest merit, together with the Libationer among the Supervisors of the Household, jointly managed the prohibitions of that quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants of the Household: four persons; the one of highest merit, together with the Libationer among the Supervisors of the Household, jointly managed the prohibitions of that quarter.

sentences.zh: 又有通事守舍人、典事守舍人、典法守舍人員。

translations.literal: There were also Attendants for General Affairs, Custodian Attendants, and Custodian of Law Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Attendants for General Affairs, Custodian Attendants, and Custodian of Law Attendants.

sentences.zh: 庶子四人，掌侍從左右，獻納得失。

translations.literal: Junior Supervisors: four persons, who attended at the ruler's side and offered advice on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Supervisors: four persons, who attended at the ruler's side and offered advice on gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 高功者一人，與高功舍人共掌其坊之禁令。

translations.literal: The one of highest merit, together with the highly meritorious Attendant, jointly managed the prohibitions of that quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The one of highest merit, together with the highly meritorious Attendant, jointly managed the prohibitions of that quarter.

sentences.zh: 舍人十六人，掌文記。

translations.literal: Attendants: sixteen persons, who managed written records.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants: sixteen persons, who managed written records.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人二人，視南台禦史，多以餘官兼職。

translations.literal: Attendants for General Affairs: two persons, treated as equal to Southern Office Censors; many held the post concurrently with other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants for General Affairs: two persons, treated as equal to Southern Office Censors; many held the post concurrently with other offices.

sentences.zh: 典經局洗馬八人，位視通直郎。

translations.literal: Masters of the Classics Bureau: eight persons, rank equal to Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of the Classics Bureau: eight persons, rank equal to Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 置典經守舍人、典事守舍人員。

translations.literal: Custodian Attendants of the Classics Bureau and Custodian Attendants for Affairs were established.
translations.idiomatic: Custodian Attendants of the Classics Bureau and Custodian Attendants for Affairs were established.

sentences.zh: 又有外監殿局，內監殿局，導客局，齋內局，主璽、主衣、扶侍等局，門局，錫庫局，內廄局，中藥藏局，食官局，外廄局，車廄局等，各置有司，以承其事。

translations.literal: There were also the Outer Supervisory Palace Bureau, Inner Supervisory Palace Bureau, Guest Guidance Bureau, Inner Quarters Bureau, Seal-Holding Bureau, Robe-Holding Bureau, Attendance Bureau, Gate Bureau, Tin Storehouse Bureau, Inner Stable Bureau, Central Medicine Storehouse Bureau, Food Office Bureau, Outer Stable Bureau, Chariot Stable Bureau, and others; each had responsible officials to carry out the work.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Outer Supervisory Palace Bureau, Inner Supervisory Palace Bureau, Guest Guidance Bureau, Inner Quarters Bureau, Seal-Holding Bureau, Robe-Holding Bureau, Attendance Bureau, Gate Bureau, Tin Storehouse Bureau, Inner Stable Bureau, Central Medicine Storehouse Bureau, Food Office Bureau, Outer Stable Bureau, Chariot Stable Bureau, and others; each had responsible officials to carry out the work.

sentences.zh: 皇弟、皇子府，置師，長史，司馬，從事中郎，諮議參軍，及掾屬中錄事、中記室、中直兵等參軍，功曹史，錄事、記室、中兵等參軍，文學，主簿，正參軍、行參軍、長兼行參軍等員。

translations.literal: For the households of imperial younger brothers and princes there were established Tutor, Chief Administrator, Major, Attendant Secretary, Advisory Aide, and Aides including Central Recorder, Central Recorder of Affairs, Central Direct Military Aide, Merit Clerk, Recorder, Central Military Aide, Literary Scholar, Chief Clerk, Regular Aide, Acting Aide, and Senior Concurrent Acting Aide.
translations.idiomatic: For the households of imperial younger brothers and princes there were established Tutor, Chief Administrator, Major, Attendant Secretary, Advisory Aide, and Aides including Central Recorder, Central Recorder of Affairs, Central Direct Military Aide, Merit Clerk, Recorder, Central Military Aide, Literary Scholar, Chief Clerk, Regular Aide, Acting Aide, and Senior Concurrent Acting Aide.

sentences.zh: 嗣王府則減皇弟皇子府師、友、文學、長兼行參軍。

translations.literal: For successor princes' households, the Tutor, Friend, Literary Scholar, and Senior Concurrent Acting Aide of the imperial younger brother and prince households were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: For successor princes' households, the Tutor, Friend, Literary Scholar, and Senior Concurrent Acting Aide of the imperial younger brother and prince households were reduced.

sentences.zh: 蕃王府則又減嗣王從事中郎，諮議參軍，掾屬錄事、記室、中兵參軍等員。

translations.literal: For feudal princes' households, the Attendant Secretary, Advisory Aide, and Recorder, Recorder of Affairs, and Central Military Aides of successor princes were further reduced.
translations.idiomatic: For feudal princes' households, the Attendant Secretary, Advisory Aide, and Recorder, Recorder of Affairs, and Central Military Aides of successor princes were further reduced.

sentences.zh: 自此以下，則並不登二品。

translations.literal: From this level downward, none ranked in the second grade.
translations.idiomatic: From this level downward, none ranked in the second grade.

sentences.zh: 王國置郎中令、將軍、常侍官。

translations.literal: Princely states established Directors of Gentlemen, Generals, and Regular Attendant officials.
translations.idiomatic: Princely states established Directors of Gentlemen, Generals, and Regular Attendant officials.

sentences.zh: 又置典祠令、廟長、陵長、典醫丞、典府丞、典書令、學官令、食官長、中尉、侍郎、執事中尉、司馬、謁者、典衛令、舍人、中大夫、大農等官。

translations.literal: They also established Directors of Sacrificial Affairs, Temple Chiefs, Tomb Chiefs, Directors of the Medical Bureau, Directors of the Treasury Bureau, Directors of Documents, Directors of the Academy, Chiefs of the Food Office, Central Commandant, Vice Director, Acting Central Commandant, Major, Herald, Director of the Guard Bureau, Attendant, Grand Master, and Grand Agriculture officials.
translations.idiomatic: They also established Directors of Sacrificial Affairs, Temple Chiefs, Tomb Chiefs, Directors of the Medical Bureau, Directors of the Treasury Bureau, Directors of Documents, Directors of the Academy, Chiefs of the Food Office, Central Commandant, Vice Director, Acting Central Commandant, Major, Herald, Director of the Guard Bureau, Attendant, Grand Master, and Grand Agriculture officials.

sentences.zh: 嗣王國則唯置郎中令、中尉、常侍、大農等員。

translations.literal: Successor princely states had only Directors of Gentlemen, Central Commandant, Regular Attendant, and Grand Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Successor princely states had only Directors of Gentlemen, Central Commandant, Regular Attendant, and Grand Agriculture, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 蕃王則無常侍。

translations.literal: Feudal princes had no Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal princes had no Regular Attendant, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 自此以下，並不登二品。

translations.literal: From this level downward, none ranked in the second grade.
translations.idiomatic: From this level downward, none ranked in the second grade, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 諸王皆假金獸符第一至第五左，竹使符第一至第十左。

translations.literal: All princes were granted gold beast talismans of the first through fifth ranks on the left, and bamboo envoy talismans of the first through tenth ranks on the left.
translations.idiomatic: All princes were granted gold beast talismans of the first through fifth ranks on the left, and bamboo envoy talismans of the first through tenth ranks on the left, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 諸公侯皆假銅獸符，竹使符第一至第五。

translations.literal: All dukes and marquises were granted bronze beast talismans and bamboo envoy talismans of the first through fifth ranks.
translations.idiomatic: All dukes and marquises were granted bronze beast talismans and bamboo envoy talismans of the first through fifth ranks, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 名山大澤不以封。

translations.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes were not granted as fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Famous mountains and great marshes were not granted as fiefs, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵金銀銅錫，及竹園別都，宮室園圃，皆不以屬國。

translations.literal: Salt, iron, gold, silver, copper, and tin, as well as bamboo groves and separate commanderies, palace buildings and gardens, were none of them assigned to princely states.
translations.idiomatic: Salt, iron, gold, silver, copper, and tin, as well as bamboo groves and separate commanderies, palace buildings and gardens, were none of them assigned to princely states, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 諸王言曰令，境內稱之曰殿下。

translations.literal: Princes addressed themselves as "Command"; within their domains they were addressed as "Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Princes addressed themselves as "Command"; within their domains they were addressed as "Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 公侯封郡縣者，言曰教，境內稱之曰第下。

translations.literal: Dukes and marquises enfeoffed with commanderies and counties addressed themselves as "Instruction"; within their domains they were addressed as "Your Residence."
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises enfeoffed with commanderies and counties addressed themselves as "Instruction"; within their domains they were addressed as "Your Residence."

sentences.zh: 自稱皆曰寡人。

translations.literal: They all addressed themselves as "I, the unworthy one."
translations.idiomatic: They all addressed themselves as "I, the unworthy one."

sentences.zh: 相以下，公文上事，皆詣典書。

translations.literal: Below the Chancellor, all official documents and reports were submitted to the Director of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Chancellor, all official documents and reports were submitted to the Director of Documents, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 世子主國，其文書表疏，儀式如臣而不稱臣。

translations.literal: When the heir governed the state, his documents and memorials followed the forms of a minister but did not call himself minister.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the heir governed the state, his documents and memorials followed the forms of a minister but did not call himself minister.

sentences.zh: 文書下群官，皆言告。

translations.literal: Documents issued to subordinate officials all said "Proclamation."
translations.idiomatic: Documents issued to subordinate officials all said "Proclamation."

sentences.zh: 諸王公侯國官，皆稱臣。
