translations.literal: All officials of princely, ducal, and marquis states called themselves ministers.
translations.idiomatic: All officials of princely, ducal, and marquis states called themselves ministers, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 上於天朝，皆稱陪臣。

translations.literal: When appearing at the imperial court, all called themselves accompanying ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Upon appearing at the imperial court, all called themselves accompanying ministers.

sentences.zh: 有所陳，皆曰上疏。

translations.literal: When making representations, all said "Submitting a memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Upon making representations, all said "Submitting a memorial."

sentences.zh: 其公文曰言事。

translations.literal: Their official documents said "Reporting an affair."
translations.idiomatic: Their official documents said "Reporting an affair."

sentences.zh: 五等諸公，位視三公，班次之。

translations.literal: Dukes of the five ranks: rank equal to the Three Excellencies, precedence next after them.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes of the five ranks—rank equal to the Three Excellencies, precedence next after them.

sentences.zh: 開皇諸侯，位視孤卿、重號將軍、光祿大夫，班次之。

translations.literal: Marquises who founded states under Kaihuang: rank equal to Solitary Ministers, Heavy-Titled Generals, and Masters of Brilliant Happiness; precedence next after them.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises who founded states under Kaihuang—rank equal to Solitary Ministers, Heavy-Titled Generals, and Masters of Brilliant Happiness; precedence next after them.

sentences.zh: 開國諸伯，位視九卿，班次之。

translations.literal: Earls who founded states: rank equal to the Nine Ministers; precedence next after them.
translations.idiomatic: Earls who founded states—rank equal to the Nine Ministers; precedence next after them.

sentences.zh: 開國諸子，位視二千石，班次之。

translations.literal: Viscounts who founded states: rank equal to two-thousand-shi; precedence next after them.
translations.idiomatic: Viscounts who founded states—rank equal to two-thousand-shi; precedence next after them.

sentences.zh: 開國諸男，位視比二千石，班次之。

translations.literal: Barons who founded states: rank equal to equivalent two-thousand-shi; precedence next after them.
translations.idiomatic: Barons who founded states—rank equal to equivalent two-thousand-shi; precedence next after them.

sentences.zh: 公已下，各置相、典祠、典書令、典衛長一人。

translations.literal: From dukes downward, each established one Chancellor, Director of Sacrificial Affairs, Director of Documents, and Chief of the Guard Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: From dukes downward, each established one Chancellor, Director of Sacrificial Affairs, Director of Documents, and Chief of the Guard Bureau, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 而伯子典書謂之長，典衛謂之丞。

translations.literal: For earls and viscounts, Director of Documents was called Chief and Chief of the Guard Bureau was called Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: For earls and viscounts, Director of Documents was called Chief and Chief of the Guard Bureau was called Assistant Director, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 男典祠謂之長，典書謂之丞，無典衛。

translations.literal: For barons, Director of Sacrificial Affairs was called Chief, Director of Documents was called Assistant Director, and there was no Chief of the Guard Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: For barons, Director of Sacrificial Affairs was called Chief, Director of Documents was called Assistant Director, and there was no Chief of the Guard Bureau, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 諸公已下，台為選置相，掌知百姓事。

translations.literal: From dukes downward, the central offices selected and appointed the Chancellor, who managed the affairs of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: From dukes downward, the central offices selected and appointed the Chancellor, who managed the affairs of the common people, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 典祠已下，自選補上。

translations.literal: From Director of Sacrificial Affairs downward, they selected and filled posts themselves.
translations.idiomatic: From Director of Sacrificial Affairs downward, they selected and filled posts themselves, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 諸列侯食邑千戶已上，置家丞、庶子員。

translations.literal: For all ranked marquises with fiefs of one thousand households or more, Household Assistant and Junior Supervisor posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: Every ranked marquises with fiefs of one thousand households or more, Household Assistant and Junior Supervisor posts were established.

sentences.zh: 不滿千戶，則但置庶子員。

translations.literal: For those with fewer than one thousand households, only a Junior Supervisor was established.
translations.idiomatic: For those with fewer than one thousand households, only a Junior Supervisor was established, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 州刺史二千石，受拜之明日，辭宮廟而行。

translations.literal: Prefects of provinces at two-thousand-shi rank, on the day after receiving appointment, paid respects at the ancestral temple and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects of provinces at two-thousand-shi rank, on the day after receiving appointment, paid respects at the ancestral temple and then departed, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 州置別駕、治中從事各一人，主簿，西曹、議曹從事，祭酒從事，部傳從事，文學從事，各因其州之大小而置員。

translations.literal: Provinces established one Administrative Aide and one Supervising Aide each, a Chief Clerk, Western Bureau Aide, Advisory Aide, Libationer Aide, Dispatch Aide, and Literary Aide—the number of each depending on the size of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces established one Administrative Aide and one Supervising Aide each, a Chief Clerk, Western Bureau Aide, Advisory Aide, Libationer Aide, Dispatch Aide, and Literary Aide—the number of each depending on the size of the province, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 郡置太守，置丞。

translations.literal: Commanderies established a Grand Administrator and an Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies established a Grand Administrator and an Assistant Director, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 國曰內史。

translations.literal: Princely states were called Inner Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Princely states were called Inner Secretaries, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 郡丞，三萬戶以上，置佐一人。

translations.literal: For commandery Assistant Directors, in commanderies of thirty thousand households or more, one Assistant was established.
translations.idiomatic: For commandery Assistant Directors, in commanderies of thirty thousand households or more, one Assistant was established, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 縣為國曰相，大縣為令，小縣為長，皆置丞、尉。

translations.literal: Counties in princely states were called Chancellors; large counties had Magistrates and small counties had Chiefs—all with Assistant Directors and Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Counties in princely states were called Chancellors; large counties had Magistrates and small counties had Chiefs—all with Assistant Directors and Commandants, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 郡縣置吏，亦各准州法，以大小而制員。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties established clerks according to provincial regulations, with numbers determined by size.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies and counties established clerks according to provincial regulations, with numbers determined by size, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 郡縣吏有書僮，有武吏，有醫，有迎新、送故等員。

translations.literal: Commandery and county clerks included scribes, military clerks, physicians, and posts for welcoming new officials and seeing off departing ones.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery and county clerks included scribes, military clerks, physicians, and posts for welcoming new officials and seeing off departing ones, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 亦各因其大小而置焉。

translations.literal: The number of each also depended on size.
translations.idiomatic: The number of each also depended on size, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 天監初，武帝命尚書刪定郎濟陽蔡法度，定令為九品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, Emperor Wu ordered Cai Fadu, Director of Review and Fixation in the Department of State Affairs, to fix the ordinances into nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian, Emperor Wu ordered Cai Fadu, Director of Review and Fixation in the Department of State Affairs, to fix the ordinances into nine grades, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 秩定，帝於品下注一品秩為萬石，第二第三為中二千石，第四第五為二千石。

translations.literal: When the ranks were fixed, the emperor annotated the first grade as ten-thousand-shi, the second and third as middle two-thousand-shi, and the fourth and fifth as two-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the ranks were fixed, the emperor annotated the first grade as ten-thousand-shi, the second and third as middle two-thousand-shi, and the fourth and fifth as two-thousand-shi.

sentences.zh: 至七年，革選，徐勉為吏部尚書，定為十八班。

translations.literal: By the seventh year, when selections were reformed, Xu Mian as Minister of Personnel fixed them as eighteen classes.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh year, when selections were reformed, Xu Mian as Minister of Personnel fixed them as eighteen classes, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 以班多者為貴，同班者，則以居下者為劣。

translations.literal: Those with more classes were more honored; where classes were equal, the one lower in the list was inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Those with more classes were more honored; where classes were equal, the one lower in the list was inferior, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 丞相、太宰、太傅、太保、大司馬、大將軍、太尉、司徒、司空，為十八班。

translations.literal: Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, and Minister of Works: eighteen classes.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, and Minister of Works. These offices belonged to the eighteen class.

sentences.zh: 諸將軍開府儀同三司、左右光祿開府儀同三司，為十七班。

translations.literal: Generals who opened offices with equal privilege to the Three Excellencies, and Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness who opened such offices: seventeen classes.
translations.idiomatic: Generals who opened offices with equal privilege to the Three Excellencies, and Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness who opened such offices. These offices belonged to the seventeen class.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、太子太傅、左右光祿大夫，為十六班。

translations.literal: Director of the Department of State Affairs, Crown Prince's Grand Tutor, and Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness: sixteen classes.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Department of State Affairs, Crown Prince's Grand Tutor, and Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness. These offices belonged to the sixteen class.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射，太子少傅，尚書僕射、右僕射，中書監，特進，領、護軍將軍，為十五班。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Crown Prince's Junior Tutor, Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, Supervisor of the Secretariat, Special Advancement, Commander-in-Chief, and Protector-General: fifteen classes.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Crown Prince's Junior Tutor, Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, Supervisor of the Secretariat, Special Advancement, Commander-in-Chief, and Protector-General. These offices belonged to the fifteen class.

sentences.zh: 中領、護軍，吏部尚書，太子詹事，金紫光祿大夫，太常卿，為十四班。

translations.literal: Central Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General, Minister of Personnel, Superintendent of the Crown Prince's Household, Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, and Minister of Ceremonies: fourteen classes.
translations.idiomatic: Central Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General, Minister of Personnel, Superintendent of the Crown Prince's Household, Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, and Minister of Ceremonies. These offices belonged to the fourteen class.

sentences.zh: 中書令，列曹尚書，國子祭酒，宗正、太府卿，光祿大夫，為十三班。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat, Ministers of the various departments, National Academy Libationer, Ministers of the Imperial Clan and Palace Treasury, and Master of Brilliant Happiness: thirteen classes.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat, Ministers of the various departments, National Academy Libationer, Ministers of the Imperial Clan and Palace Treasury, and Master of Brilliant Happiness. These offices belonged to the thirteen class.

sentences.zh: 侍中，散騎常侍，左、右衛將軍，司徒左長史，衛尉卿，為十二班。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Left and Right Guard Generals, Left Chief Administrator of the Minister over the Masses, and Commandant of the Guards: twelve classes.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Left and Right Guard Generals, Left Chief Administrator of the Minister over the Masses, and Commandant of the Guards. These offices belonged to the twelve class.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞，尚書吏部郎，秘書監，通直散騎常侍，太子左、右二衛率，左、右驍騎，左、右遊擊，太中大夫，皇弟皇子師，司農，少府、廷尉卿，太子中庶子，光祿卿，為十一班。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief, Director of Personnel in the Department of State Affairs, Supervisor of the Imperial Library, Direct Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Left and Right Commandants of the Crown Prince's Guard, Left and Right Valiant Cavalry, Left and Right Mobile Attack, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Tutors of imperial younger brothers and princes, Minister of the Grand Granary, Ministers of the Palace Stores and Punishments, Supervisors of the Crown Prince's Household, and Minister of Brilliant Happiness: eleven classes.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief, Director of Personnel in the Department of State Affairs, Supervisor of the Imperial Library, Direct Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Left and Right Commandants of the Crown Prince's Guard, Left and Right Valiant Cavalry, Left and Right Mobile Attack, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Tutors of imperial younger brothers and princes, Minister of the Grand Granary, Ministers of the Palace Stores and Punishments, Supervisors of the Crown Prince's Household, and Minister of Brilliant Happiness. These offices belonged to the eleven class.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎，員外散騎常侍，皇弟皇子府長史，太僕、大匠卿，太子家令、率更令、僕，揚州別駕，中散大夫，司徒右長史，雲騎，遊騎，皇弟皇子府司馬，硃衣直閣將軍，為十班。

translations.literal: Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate, Extra Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Chief Administrator of imperial younger brother and prince households, Ministers of the Imperial Stud and Construction, Directors of the Crown Prince's Household, Commandant of the Watch and Gate, and Steward, Yangzhou Administrative Aide, Master of Palace Attendance, Right Chief Administrator of the Minister over the Masses, Cloud Cavalry and Mobile Cavalry Generals, Major of imperial younger brother and prince households, and Scarlet-Robed Direct Gate General: ten classes.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate, Extra Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Chief Administrator of imperial younger brother and prince households, Ministers of the Imperial Stud and Construction, Directors of the Crown Prince's Household, Commandant of the Watch and Gate, and Steward, Yangzhou Administrative Aide, Master of Palace Attendance, Right Chief Administrator of the Minister over the Masses, Cloud Cavalry and Mobile Cavalry Generals, Major of imperial younger brother and prince households, and Scarlet-Robed Direct Gate General. These offices belonged to the ten class.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞，鴻臚卿，中書侍郎，國子博士，太子庶子，揚州中從事，皇弟皇子公府從事中郎，太舟卿，大長秋，皇弟皇子府諮議，嗣王府長史，前左右後四軍、嗣王府司馬，庶姓公府長史，司馬，為九班。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, Minister of the Grand Herald, Secretary of the Secretariat, National Academy Erudite, Junior Supervisor of the Crown Prince, Yangzhou Supervising Aide, Attendant Secretary of imperial younger brother and ducal households, Minister of Great Vessels, Grand Director of the Palace Domain, Advisory Aide of imperial younger brother and prince households, Chief Administrator of successor princes' households, Front, Left, Right, and Rear Four Generals and Major of successor princes' households, Chief Administrator and Major of commoner ducal households: nine classes.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, Minister of the Grand Herald, Secretary of the Secretariat, National Academy Erudite, Junior Supervisor of the Crown Prince, Yangzhou Supervising Aide, Attendant Secretary of imperial younger brother and ducal households, Minister of Great Vessels, Grand Director of the Palace Domain, Advisory Aide of imperial younger brother and prince households, Chief Administrator of successor princes' households, Front, Left, Right, and Rear Four Generals and Major of successor princes' households, Chief Administrator and Major of commoner ducal households. These offices belonged to the nine class.

sentences.zh: 秘書丞，太子中舍人，司徒左西掾，司徒屬，皇弟皇子友，散騎侍郎，尚書右丞，南徐州別駕，皇弟皇子公府掾屬，皇弟皇子單為二衛司馬，嗣王庶姓公府從事中郎，左、右中郎將，嗣王庶姓公府諮議，皇弟皇子之庶子府長史、司馬，蕃王府長史、司馬，庶姓持節府長史、司馬，為八班。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Imperial Library, Attendant of the Crown Prince's Household, Left Western Secretary and Secretary of the Minister over the Masses, Friend of imperial younger brothers and princes, Gentleman of the Loose Retinue, Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, Southern Xuzhou Administrative Aide, Staff Secretary of imperial younger brother and ducal households, Major of imperial younger brother and prince households serving solely as Two Guard Majors, Attendant Secretary of successor and commoner ducal households, Left and Right Commandants of the Central Guard, Advisory Aide of successor and commoner ducal households, Chief Administrator and Major of junior prince and commoner ducal households, Chief Administrator and Major of feudal princes' households, and Chief Administrator and Major of commoner households holding staff of authority: eight classes.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of the Imperial Library, Attendant of the Crown Prince's Household, Left Western Secretary and Secretary of the Minister over the Masses, Friend of imperial younger brothers and princes, Gentleman of the Loose Retinue, Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, Southern Xuzhou Administrative Aide, Staff Secretary of imperial younger brother and ducal households, Major of imperial younger brother and prince households serving solely as Two Guard Majors, Attendant Secretary of successor and commoner ducal households, Left and Right Commandants of the Central Guard, Advisory Aide of successor and commoner ducal households, Chief Administrator and Major of junior prince and commoner ducal households, Chief Administrator and Major of feudal princes' households, and Chief Administrator and Major of commoner households holding staff of authority. These offices belonged to the eight class.

sentences.zh: 五校，東宮三校，皇弟皇子之庶子府中錄事、中記室、中直兵參軍，南徐州中從事，皇弟皇子之庶子府、蕃王府諮議，為七班。

translations.literal: Five Commandants, Three Commandants of the Eastern Palace, Central Recorder, Central Recorder of Affairs, and Central Direct Military Aides of junior prince households, Southern Xuzhou Supervising Aide, and Advisory Aides of junior prince and feudal princes' households: seven classes.
translations.idiomatic: Five Commandants, Three Commandants of the Eastern Palace, Central Recorder, Central Recorder of Affairs, and Central Direct Military Aides of junior prince households, Southern Xuzhou Supervising Aide, and Advisory Aides of junior prince and feudal princes' households. These offices belonged to the seven class.

sentences.zh: 太子洗馬，通直散騎侍郎，司徒主簿，尚書侍郎，著作郎，皇弟皇子府功曹史，五經博士，皇弟皇子府錄事、記室、中兵參軍，皇弟皇子荊江雍郢南兗五州別駕，領、護軍長史、司馬，嗣王庶姓公府掾屬，南台治書侍御史，廷尉三官，謁者僕射，太子門大夫，嗣王庶姓公府中錄事、中記室、中直兵參軍，庶姓府諮議，為六班。

translations.literal: Master of the Classics Bureau of the Crown Prince, Direct Regular Gentleman of the Loose Retinue, Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses, Secretary of the Department of State Affairs, Master of Writing, Merit Clerk of imperial younger brother and prince households, Erudite of the Five Classics, Recorder, Recorder of Affairs, and Central Military Aides of imperial younger brother and prince households, Administrative Aides of Jing, Jiang, Yong, Ying, and Southern Yanzhou for imperial younger brothers and princes, Chief Administrator and Major of Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General households, Staff Secretary of successor and commoner ducal households, Southern Office Supervising Censor, Three Officials of the Commandant of Punishments, Vice Director of Heralds, Gate Grand Master of the Crown Prince, Central Recorder, Central Recorder of Affairs, and Central Direct Military Aides of successor and commoner ducal households, and Advisory Aide of commoner households: six classes.
translations.idiomatic: Master of the Classics Bureau of the Crown Prince, Direct Regular Gentleman of the Loose Retinue, Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses, Secretary of the Department of State Affairs, Master of Writing, Merit Clerk of imperial younger brother and prince households, Erudite of the Five Classics, Recorder, Recorder of Affairs, and Central Military Aides of imperial younger brother and prince households, Administrative Aides of Jing, Jiang, Yong, Ying, and Southern Yanzhou for imperial younger brothers and princes, Chief Administrator and Major of Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General households, Staff Secretary of successor and commoner ducal households, Southern Office Supervising Censor, Three Officials of the Commandant of Punishments, Vice Director of Heralds, Gate Grand Master of the Crown Prince, Central Recorder, Central Recorder of Affairs, and Central Direct Military Aides of successor and commoner ducal households, and Advisory Aide of commoner households. These offices belonged to the six class.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎中，皇弟皇子文學及府主簿，太子太傅、少傅丞，皇弟皇子湘豫司益廣青衡七州別駕，皇弟皇子荊江雍郢南兗五州中從事，嗣王庶姓荊江雍郢南兗五州別駕，太常丞，皇弟皇子國郎中令、三將，東宮二將，嗣王府功曹史，庶姓公府錄事、記室、中兵參軍，皇弟皇子之庶子府、蕃王府中錄事、中記室、中直兵參軍，為五班。

translations.literal: Cross the Barrier, Offer Transformation, Healthy Righteousness, Surpass Longxi, and Raise Transformation were the same class, modeled on the titles of Fierce Assault and others.
translations.idiomatic: Cross the Barrier, Offer Transformation, Healthy Righteousness, Surpass Longxi, and Raise Transformation were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Fierce Assault and others.

sentences.zh: 甯關、橫沙、雄邊、振隴、平河同班，擬忠勇等號。

translations.literal: Tranquilize the Pass, Cross the Sands, Heroic Border, Quell Longxi, and Pacify the River were the same class, modeled on the titles of Loyal Valor and others.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquilize the Pass, Cross the Sands, Heroic Border, Quell Longxi, and Pacify the River were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Loyal Valor and others.

sentences.zh: 鑿空、浮遼、弘節、宣義、懷信同班，擬明智等號。

translations.literal: Bore the Void, Float Distant, Propagate Restraint, Proclaim Righteousness, and Cherish Trust were the same class, modeled on the titles of Bright Wisdom and others.
translations.idiomatic: Bore the Void, Float Distant, Propagate Restraint, Proclaim Righteousness, and Cherish Trust were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Bright Wisdom and others.

sentences.zh: 明信、陵河、歸義、款塞、捍海同班，擬光烈等號。

translations.literal: Bright Trust, Cross the River, Return to Righteousness, Win Over the Frontier, and Defend the Sea were the same class, modeled on the titles of Glorious Assault and others.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Trust, Cross the River, Return to Righteousness, Win Over the Frontier, and Defend the Sea were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Glorious Assault and others.

sentences.zh: 立義、仰化、弘信、守義、奉忠同班，擬飆勇等號。

translations.literal: Establish Righteousness, Look Up to Transformation, Propagate Trust, Guard Righteousness, and Uphold Loyalty were the same class, modeled on the titles of Storm Valor and others.
translations.idiomatic: Establish Righteousness, Look Up to Transformation, Propagate Trust, Guard Righteousness, and Uphold Loyalty were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Storm Valor and others.

sentences.zh: 奉誠、立誠、建誠、顯誠、義誠同班，擬龍驤等號。

translations.literal: Uphold Sincerity, Establish Sincerity, Build Sincerity, Display Sincerity, and Righteous Sincerity were the same class, modeled on the titles of Dragon Charger and others.
translations.idiomatic: Uphold Sincerity, Establish Sincerity, Build Sincerity, Display Sincerity, and Righteous Sincerity were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Dragon Charger and others.

sentences.zh: 尉遼、寧渤、綏嶺、威塞、通侯同班，擬折沖等號。

translations.literal: Pacify Liao, Tranquilize Bo, Pacify the Ridge, Prestige Frontier, and Pass the Marches were the same class, modeled on the titles of Break the Ranks and others.
translations.idiomatic: Pacify Liao, Tranquilize Bo, Pacify the Ridge, Prestige Frontier, and Pass the Marches were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Break the Ranks and others.

sentences.zh: 掃荒、威荒、定荒、開荒、理荒同班，擬開遠等號。

translations.literal: Sweep the Wilderness, Prestige Wilderness, Settle the Wilderness, Open the Wilderness, and Govern the Wilderness were the same class, modeled on the titles of Open Distant and others.
translations.idiomatic: Sweep the Wilderness, Prestige Wilderness, Settle the Wilderness, Open the Wilderness, and Govern the Wilderness were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Open Distant and others.

sentences.zh: 奉節、掃節、建節、效節、伏節同班，擬超武等號。

translations.literal: Uphold Restraint, Sweep Restraint, Establish Restraint, Effect Restraint, and Submit Restraint were the same class, modeled on the titles of Super Martial and others.
translations.idiomatic: Uphold Restraint, Sweep Restraint, Establish Restraint, Effect Restraint, and Submit Restraint were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Super Martial and others.

sentences.zh: 渡河、陵海、承化、奉正、綏方同班，擬伏波等號。

translations.literal: Cross the River, Cross the Sea, Receive Transformation, Uphold Rectitude, and Pacify the Region were the same class, modeled on the titles of Subdue the Waves and others.
translations.idiomatic: Cross the River, Cross the Sea, Receive Transformation, Uphold Rectitude, and Pacify the Region were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Subdue the Waves and others.

sentences.zh: 伏義、懷澤、歸誠、奉信、懷義同班，擬前鋒等號。

translations.literal: Subdue Righteousness, Cherish Grace, Return in Sincerity, Uphold Trust, and Cherish Righteousness were the same class, modeled on the titles of Vanguard and others.
translations.idiomatic: Subdue Righteousness, Cherish Grace, Return in Sincerity, Uphold Trust, and Cherish Righteousness were the same class, corresponding to the titles of Vanguard and others.

sentences.zh: 凡一百二十五將軍，二十八班，並施外國戎號，准於中夏焉。

translations.literal: In all one hundred twenty-five generals, twenty-eight classes, all conferred on foreign barbarian titles, equivalent to those of central China.
translations.idiomatic: In all one hundred twenty-five generals, twenty-eight classes, all conferred on foreign barbarian titles, equivalent to those of central China, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 大同四年，魏彭城王爾硃仲遠來降，以為定洛大將軍，仍使其北討，故名云。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, Erzhu Zhongyuan, Prince of Pengcheng of Wei, came over in surrender and was made Grand General of Settling Luoyang; he was still sent north to campaign, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong, Erzhu Zhongyuan, Prince of Pengcheng of Wei, came over in surrender and was made Grand General of Settling Luoyang; he was still sent north to campaign, hence the name, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 陳承梁，皆循其制官，而又置相國，位列丞相上。

translations.literal: Chen succeeded Liang and all followed its institutional offices; they also established a Chancellor of State, ranking above the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen succeeded Liang and all followed its institutional offices; they also established a Chancellor of State, ranking above the Chancellor, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 並丞相、太宰、太傅、太保、大司馬、大將軍，並以為贈官。

translations.literal: Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand Marshal, and Grand General were all posthumous offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand Marshal, and Grand General were all posthumous offices, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 定令，尚書置五員，郎二十一員。

translations.literal: When the ordinances were fixed, the Department of State Affairs had five Ministers and twenty-one Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the ordinances were fixed, the Department of State Affairs had five Ministers and twenty-one Directors.

sentences.zh: 其餘並遵梁制，為十八班，而官有清濁。

translations.literal: The rest all followed the Liang system of eighteen classes, and offices were distinguished as pure or impure.
translations.idiomatic: The rest all followed the Liang system of eighteen classes, and offices were distinguished as pure or impure, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 自十二班以上並詔授，表啟不稱姓。

translations.literal: From the twelfth class upward all were appointed by edict; memorials and reports did not use surnames.
translations.idiomatic: From the twelfth class upward all were appointed by edict; memorials and reports did not use surnames, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 從十一班至九班，禮數複為一等。

translations.literal: From the eleventh class to the ninth class, ceremonial treatment formed another grade.
translations.idiomatic: From the eleventh class to the ninth class, ceremonial treatment formed another grade, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 又流外有七班，此是寒微士人為之。

translations.literal: Outside the regular ranks there were seven classes; these were held by men of humble origin.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the regular ranks there were seven classes; these were held by men of humble origin, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 從此班者，方得進登第一班。

translations.literal: Only from this class could one advance to the first class.
translations.idiomatic: Only from this class could one advance to the first class, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其親王起家則為侍中。

translations.literal: Imperial princes began office as Attendants-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes began office as Attendants-in-Ordinary, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 若加將軍，方得有佐史，無將軍則無府，止有國官。

translations.literal: If a general's title was added, then staff clerks were permitted; without a general's title there was no office, only state officials.
translations.idiomatic: Where a general's title was added, then staff clerks were permitted; without a general's title there was no office, only state officials.

sentences.zh: 皇太子塚嫡者，起家封王，依諸王起家。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's eldest son by the primary consort began office enfeoffed as a prince, following the same entry as other princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's eldest son by the primary consort began office enfeoffed as a prince, following the same entry as other princes, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 余子並封公，起家中書郎。

translations.literal: Other sons were all enfeoffed as dukes and began office as Secretaries of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Other sons were all enfeoffed as dukes and began office as Secretaries of the Secretariat, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 諸王子並諸侯世子，起家給事。

translations.literal: All princes' sons and all marquises' heirs began office as Gentlemen for Attending to Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: All princes' sons and all marquises' heirs began office as Gentlemen for Attending to Affairs, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 三公子起家員外散騎侍郎，令僕子起家秘書郎。

translations.literal: Sons of Directors and Vice Directors began office as Extra Gentlemen of the Loose Retinue; sons of Directors began office as Secretaries of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Directors and Vice Directors began office as Extra Gentlemen of the Loose Retinue; sons of Directors began office as Secretaries of the Imperial Library, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 若員滿，亦為板法曹，雖高半階，望終秘書郎下。

translations.literal: If the quota was full, they became provisional Legal Bureau Aides; though half a class higher, they ultimately ranked below Secretaries of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: Where the quota was full, they became provisional Legal Bureau Aides; though half a class higher, they ultimately ranked below Secretaries of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 次令僕子起家著作佐郎，亦為板行參軍。

translations.literal: Next, sons of Vice Directors began office as Assistant Masters of Writing, also as provisional Acting Aides.
translations.idiomatic: Next, sons of Vice Directors began office as Assistant Masters of Writing, also as provisional Acting Aides, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 此外有揚州主簿、太學博士、王國侍郎、奉朝請、嗣王行參軍，並起家官，未合發詔。

translations.literal: Beyond these there were Yangzhou Chief Clerks, Imperial Academy Erudites, Vice Directors of princely states, Court Attendants, and Acting Aides of successor princes—all entry-level offices not yet subject to edict.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these there were Yangzhou Chief Clerks, Imperial Academy Erudites, Vice Directors of princely states, Court Attendants, and Acting Aides of successor princes—all entry-level offices not yet subject to edict, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 諸王公參佐等官，仍為清濁。

translations.literal: Staff and aides of all princes and dukes were still distinguished as pure or impure.
translations.idiomatic: Staff and aides of all princes and dukes were still distinguished as pure or impure, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 或有選司補用，亦有府牒即授者，不拘年限，去留隨意。

translations.literal: Some were appointed by the selection office; some received appointment directly from the household document—without regard to term limits, departure and retention at will.
translations.idiomatic: Some were appointed by the selection office; some received appointment directly from the household document—without regard to term limits, departure and retention at will, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 在府之日，唯賓遊宴賞，時複修參，更無餘事。

translations.literal: While in the household, they only joined in guest banquets and entertainments, occasionally attending to official business; there were no other duties.
translations.idiomatic: While in the household, they only joined in guest banquets and entertainments, occasionally attending to official business; there were no other duties, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 若隨府王在州，其僚佐等，或亦得預催督。

translations.literal: If they followed the prince to his province, their staff and aides might also participate in supervision and urging.
translations.idiomatic: Where they followed the prince to his province, their staff and aides might also participate in supervision and urging.

sentences.zh: 若其驅使，便有職務。

translations.literal: If they were sent on missions, then they had real duties.
translations.idiomatic: Where they were sent on missions, then they had real duties.

sentences.zh: 其衣冠子弟，多自修立，非氣類者，唯利是求，暴物亂政，皆此之類。

translations.literal: Many sons of the gentry cultivated themselves; those not of the same kind sought only profit, plundering goods and disturbing government—all were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Many sons of the gentry cultivated themselves; those not of the same kind sought only profit, plundering goods and disturbing government—all were of this sort, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 國之政事，並由中書省。

translations.literal: The state's government affairs all passed through the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The state's government affairs all passed through the Secretariat, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 有中書舍人五人，領主事十人，書吏二百人。

translations.literal: There were five Secretaries of the Secretariat, ten Chief Clerks, and two hundred writing clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The administration maintained five Secretaries of the Secretariat, ten Chief Clerks, and two hundred writing clerks.

sentences.zh: 書吏不足，並取助書。

translations.literal: When writing clerks were insufficient, assistant scribes were also taken.
translations.idiomatic: Upon writing clerks were insufficient, assistant scribes were also taken.

sentences.zh: 分掌二十一局事，各當尚書諸曹，並為上司，總國內機要，而尚書唯聽受而已。

translations.literal: They divided management of twenty-one bureaus, each corresponding to the various departments of the Department of State Affairs, all serving as superiors and controlling the inner secrets of the state, while the Department of State Affairs only received and listened.
translations.idiomatic: They divided management of twenty-one bureaus, each corresponding to the various departments of the Department of State Affairs, all serving as superiors and controlling the inner secrets of the state, while the Department of State Affairs only received and listened, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 被委此官，多擅威勢。

translations.literal: Those entrusted with this office often wielded excessive power.
translations.idiomatic: Those entrusted with this office often wielded excessive power, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其庶姓為州，若無將軍者，謂之單車。

translations.literal: For commoners serving as provincial governors, if there was no general's title, they were called Single Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: For commoners serving as provincial governors, if there was no general's title, they were called Single Chariot, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 郡縣官之任代下，有迎新送故之法，餉饋皆百姓出，並以定令。

translations.literal: When commandery and county officials were replaced, there were methods for welcoming the new and seeing off the old; provisions and gifts were all supplied by the common people and were fixed by ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Upon commandery and county officials were replaced, there were methods for welcoming the new and seeing off the old; provisions and gifts were all supplied by the common people and were fixed by ordinance.

sentences.zh: 其所製品秩，今列之云。

translations.literal: The grades and ranks they established are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: The grades and ranks they established are listed below, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 相國，丞相，太宰，太傅，太保，大司馬，大將軍，太尉，司徒，司空，開府儀同三司，已上秩萬石。

translations.literal: Chancellor of State, Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, Minister of Works, and Opener of an Office with Equal Privilege to the Three Excellencies: all ranked at ten-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of State, Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, Minister of Works, and Opener of an Office with Equal Privilege to the Three Excellencies—all ranked at ten-thousand-shi and above.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王、汝陰王后，尚書令，已上秩中二千石。

translations.literal: After the kings of Baling and Yuyin, and the Director of the Department of State Affairs: all ranked at middle two-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: After the kings of Baling and Yuyin, and the Director of the Department of State Affairs—all ranked at middle two-thousand-shi and above.

sentences.zh: 品並第一。

translations.literal: All were grade one.
translations.idiomatic: All were grade one, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 中書監，尚書左右僕射，特進，太子二傅，左右光祿大夫，已上中二千石。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Secretariat, Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, Special Advancement, Crown Prince's Two Tutors, and Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness: all middle two-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Secretariat, Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, Special Advancement, Crown Prince's Two Tutors, and Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness—all middle two-thousand-shi and above.

sentences.zh: 品並第二。

translations.literal: All were grade two.
translations.idiomatic: All were grade two, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 中書令，侍中，散騎常侍，領、護軍，中領、護軍，吏部尚書，列曹尚書，金紫光祿大夫，光祿大夫，已上並中二千石。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General, Central Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General, Minister of Personnel, Ministers of the various departments, Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, and Master of Brilliant Happiness: all middle two-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General, Central Commander-in-Chief and Protector-General, Minister of Personnel, Ministers of the various departments, Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, and Master of Brilliant Happiness. All ranked at middle two-thousand-shi.

sentences.zh: 左右衛將軍，禦史中丞，已上二千石。

translations.literal: Left and Right Guard Generals and Censor-in-Chief: two-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Guard Generals and Censor-in-Chief. They received two,000 shi or more.

sentences.zh: 太後衛尉、太僕、少府三卿，太常、宗正、太府、衛尉、司農、少府、廷尉、光祿、大匠、太僕、鴻臚、太舟等卿，太子詹事，國子祭酒，已上中二千石。

translations.literal: Three ministers of the Empress Dowager's Guard, Imperial Stud, and Palace Stores; Ministers of Ceremonies, Imperial Clan, Palace Treasury, Guards, Grand Granary, Palace Stores, Punishments, Brilliant Happiness, Construction, Imperial Stud, Grand Herald, and Great Vessels; Superintendent of the Crown Prince's Household; and National Academy Libationer: all middle two-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Three ministers of the Empress Dowager's Guard, Imperial Stud, and Palace Stores; Ministers of Ceremonies, Imperial Clan, Palace Treasury, Guards, Grand Granary, Palace Stores, Punishments, Brilliant Happiness, Construction, Imperial Stud, Grand Herald, and Great Vessels; Superintendent of the Crown Prince's Household; and National Academy Libationer—all middle two-thousand-shi and above.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史，凡單車刺史，加督進一品，都督進二品。

translations.literal: Prefect of Yangzhou; for all Single Chariot prefects, adding Supervisor advanced one grade; adding Commander-in-Chief advanced two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect of Yangzhou; for all Single Chariot prefects, adding Supervisor advanced one grade; adding Commander-in-Chief advanced two grades, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 不論持節假節，揚州、徐州加督，進二品右光祿已下。

translations.literal: Regardless of holding staff of authority or seal of authority, for Yangzhou and Xuzhou adding Supervisor advanced two grades below Right Master of Brilliant Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Regardless of holding staff of authority or seal of authority, for Yangzhou and Xuzhou adding Supervisor advanced two grades below Right Master of Brilliant Happiness, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 加都督，第一品尚書令下。

translations.literal: Adding Commander-in-Chief advanced below grade-one Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Adding Commander-in-Chief advanced below grade-one Director of the Department of State Affairs, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 南徐、東揚州刺史，皇弟皇子封國王世子，品並第三。

translations.literal: Prefects of Southern Xu and Eastern Yangzhou, and heirs of imperial younger brothers, princes, enfeoffed princes, and state princes: all grade three.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects of Southern Xu and Eastern Yangzhou, and heirs of imperial younger brothers, princes, enfeoffed princes, and state princes. All were classified as grade three.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍，員外散騎常侍，黃門侍郎，已上二千石。

translations.literal: Direct Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Extra Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, and Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate: two-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, Extra Regular Attendant of the Loose Retinue, and Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate. They received two,000 shi or more.

sentences.zh: 秘書監，中二千石。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Imperial Library: middle two-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Imperial Library. They ranked at middle two-thousand-shi.

sentences.zh: 左右驍騎、左右遊擊等將軍，太子中庶子，已上二千石。

translations.literal: Left and Right Valiant Cavalry and Mobile Attack Generals and Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household: two-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Valiant Cavalry and Mobile Attack Generals and Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household. They received two,000 shi or more.

sentences.zh: 太子左右衛率，二千石硃衣直閣，雲騎、游騎將軍，中書侍郎，已上千石。

translations.literal: Left and Right Commandants of the Crown Prince's Guard: two-thousand-shi; Scarlet-Robed Direct Gate; Cloud Cavalry and Mobile Cavalry Generals; Secretary of the Secretariat: one-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Commandants of the Crown Prince's Guard: two-thousand-shi; Scarlet-Robed Direct Gate; Cloud Cavalry and Mobile Cavalry Generals; Secretary of the Secretariat. They received one,000 shi or more.

sentences.zh: 尚書左右丞，尚書、吏部侍郎、郎中，已上六百石。

translations.literal: Left and Right Assistant Directors of the Department of State Affairs, Secretaries and Directors of Personnel in the Department of State Affairs: six-hundred-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Assistant Directors of the Department of State Affairs, Secretaries and Directors of Personnel in the Department of State Affairs—six-hundred-shi and above.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎中與吏部郎同列，今品同。

translations.literal: Directors of the Department of State Affairs and Directors of Personnel were listed together; now their grades were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of the Department of State Affairs and Directors of Personnel were listed together; now their grades were the same, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 太子三卿，太中、中散大夫，司徒左右長史，已上千石。

translations.literal: Three ministers of the Crown Prince, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and Master of Palace Attendance, and Left and Right Chief Administrators of the Minister over the Masses: one-thousand-shi and above.
translations.idiomatic: Three ministers of the Crown Prince, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and Master of Palace Attendance, and Left and Right Chief Administrators of the Minister over the Masses. They received one,000 shi or more.

sentences.zh: 諸王師，依秩減之例。

translations.literal: Tutors of princes: according to the rule of reduced rank.
translations.idiomatic: Tutors of princes—according to the rule of reduced rank.

sentences.zh: 國子博士，千石。

translations.literal: National Academy Erudite: one-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: National Academy Erudite. The stipend was one,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 荊江南兗郢湘雍等州刺史，六州加督，進在第三品東揚州下。

translations.literal: Prefects of Jing, Jiang, Southern Yan, Ying, Xiang, and Yongzhou; for the six provinces adding Supervisor, advancement was below grade-three Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects of Jing, Jiang, Southern Yan, Ying, Xiang, and Yongzhou; for the six provinces adding Supervisor, advancement was below grade-three Eastern Yangzhou, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 加都督，進在第二品右光祿下。

sentences.zh: 若有將軍，減一階。

translations.literal: If there was a general's title, one grade lower.
translations.idiomatic: Where there was a general's title, one grade lower.

sentences.zh: 安遠護軍，度支校尉巴陵郡丞等，擬官二十三號，品第八。

translations.literal: Pacification Distant Protector-General, Revenue Control Commandant, and Assistant Director of Baling Commandery: twenty-three titles modeled on grade eight.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Distant Protector-General, Revenue Control Commandant, and Assistant Director of Baling Commandery—twenty-three titles modeled on grade eight.

sentences.zh: 並六百石。

translations.literal: All six-hundred-shi.
translations.idiomatic: All six-hundred-shi, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 前鋒、武毅、開邊、招遠、金威、破陣、蕩寇、殄虜、橫野、馳射等將軍，擬官十號，品第九。

translations.literal: Vanguard, Martial Resolution, Open the Border, Summon the Distant, Golden Prestige, Break the Array, Sweep the Bandits, Exterminate the Barbarians, Sweep the Wilds, and Galloping Archer Generals: ten titles modeled on grade nine.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard, Martial Resolution, Open the Border, Summon the Distant, Golden Prestige, Break the Array, Sweep the Bandits, Exterminate the Barbarians, Sweep the Wilds, and Galloping Archer Generals—ten titles modeled on grade nine.

sentences.zh: 並四百石。

translations.literal: All four-hundred-shi.
translations.idiomatic: All four-hundred-shi, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 諸將起自第六品已下，板則無秩。

translations.literal: For generals beginning from grade six downward, provisional appointment carried no rank.
translations.idiomatic: For generals beginning from grade six downward, provisional appointment carried no rank, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其雖除不領兵，領兵不滿百人，並除此官而為州郡縣者，皆依本條減秩石。

translations.literal: Even if appointed but not commanding troops, or commanding fewer than one hundred men, and then serving as provincial, commandery, or county officials—all were reduced in rank according to this article.
translations.idiomatic: Even if appointed but not commanding troops, or commanding fewer than one hundred men, and then serving as provincial, commandery, or county officials—all were reduced in rank according to this article, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 二千石減為千石，千石降為六百石。

translations.literal: Two-thousand-shi was reduced to one-thousand-shi; one-thousand-shi was reduced to six-hundred-shi.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thousand-shi was reduced to one-thousand-shi; one-thousand-shi was reduced to six-hundred-shi, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 自 四百石降而無秩。

translations.literal: From four-hundred-shi downward there was no rank.
translations.idiomatic: From four-hundred-shi downward there was no rank, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其州郡縣，自各以本秩論。

translations.literal: For provinces, commanderies, and counties, each was assessed according to its original rank.
translations.idiomatic: For provinces, commanderies, and counties, each was assessed according to its original rank, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 凡板將軍，皆降除一品。

translations.literal: For all provisional generals, one grade was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Every provisional generals, one grade was reduced.

sentences.zh: 諸依此減降品秩。

translations.literal: All reductions followed this rule of lowered grade and rank.
translations.idiomatic: All reductions followed this rule of lowered grade and rank, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其應假給章印，各依舊差，不貶奪。

translations.literal: For seals and insignia to be granted on loan, each followed the old difference and was not degraded.
translations.idiomatic: For seals and insignia to be granted on loan, each followed the old difference and was not degraded, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其封爵亦為九等之差。

translations.literal: Enfeoffments also had nine grades of difference.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffments also had nine grades of difference, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 郡王第一品。

translations.literal: Commandery prince: grade one.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery prince—grade one.

sentences.zh: 秩萬石。

translations.literal: Rank ten-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: Rank ten-thousand-shi, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 嗣王、蕃王、開國郡縣公，第二品。

translations.literal: Successor princes, feudal princes, and commandery and county dukes who founded states: grade two.
translations.idiomatic: Successor princes, feudal princes, and commandery and county dukes who founded states—grade two.

sentences.zh: 開國郡、縣侯，第三品。

translations.literal: Commandery and county marquises who founded states: grade three.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery and county marquises who founded states—grade three.

sentences.zh: 開國縣伯，第四品，並視中二千石。

translations.literal: County earls who founded states: grade four; all treated as middle two-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: County earls who founded states—grade four; all treated as middle two-thousand-shi.

sentences.zh: 開國子，第五品。

translations.literal: Viscounts who founded states: grade five.
translations.idiomatic: Viscounts who founded states—grade five.

sentences.zh: 開國男，第六品。

translations.literal: Barons who founded states: grade six.
translations.idiomatic: Barons who founded states—grade six.

sentences.zh: 並視二千石。

translations.literal: All treated as two-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: All treated as two-thousand-shi, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 湯沐食侯，第七品。

translations.literal: Marquises with bath-fief grants: grade seven.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises with bath-fief grants—grade seven.

sentences.zh: 鄉、亭侯，第八品。

translations.literal: District and hamlet marquises: grade eight.
translations.idiomatic: District and hamlet marquises—grade eight.

sentences.zh: 並視千石。

translations.literal: All treated as one-thousand-shi.
translations.idiomatic: All treated as one-thousand-shi, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 關中、關外侯，第九品。

translations.literal: Marquises within and without the passes: grade nine.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises within and without the passes—grade nine.

sentences.zh: 視六百石。

translations.literal: Treated as six-hundred-shi.
translations.idiomatic: Treated as six-hundred-shi, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 陳依梁制，年未滿三十者，不得入仕。

translations.literal: Chen followed the Liang system: those not yet thirty years of age could not enter office.
translations.idiomatic: Chen followed the Liang system—those not yet thirty years of age could not enter office.

sentences.zh: 唯經學生策試得第，諸州光迎主簿，西曹左奏及經為挽郎得仕。

translations.literal: Only students of the classics who passed the examination, chief clerks of provincial light-welcome offices, Western Bureau left memorialists, and those who had served as pallbearers could enter office.
translations.idiomatic: Only students of the classics who passed the examination, chief clerks of provincial light-welcome offices, Western Bureau left memorialists, and those who had served as pallbearers could enter office, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其諸郡，唯正王任丹陽尹經迎得出身，庶姓尹則不得。

translations.literal: Among the various commanderies, only when a legitimate prince served as Director of Danyang through light-welcome could he begin office; when a commoner served as Director, he could not.
translations.idiomatic: Among the various commanderies, only when a legitimate prince served as Director of Danyang through light-welcome could he begin office; when a commoner served as Director, he could not, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 必有奇才異行殊勳，別降恩旨敘用者，不在常例。

translations.literal: If there were unusual talent, exceptional conduct, or special merit, and separate imperial favor granted appointment, that lay outside the regular rule.
translations.idiomatic: Where there were unusual talent, exceptional conduct, or special merit, and separate imperial favor granted appointment, that lay outside the regular rule.

sentences.zh: 其相知表啟通舉者，每常有之，亦無年常考校黜陟之法。

translations.literal: Mutual recommendations through provincial memorials and reports occurred from time to time; there was also no regular annual examination for promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual recommendations through provincial memorials and reports occurred from time to time; there was also no regular annual examination for promotion and demotion, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 既不為此式，所以勤惰無辨。

translations.literal: Since this was not the established method, diligence and idleness could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Since this was not the established method, diligence and idleness could not be distinguished, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 凡選官無定期，隨闕即補，多更互遷官，未必即進班秩。

translations.literal: Selection of officials had no fixed schedule; as vacancies arose they were filled, and many were transferred among offices without necessarily advancing in class at once.
translations.idiomatic: Selection of officials had no fixed schedule; as vacancies arose they were filled, and many were transferred among offices without necessarily advancing in class at once, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其官唯論清濁，從濁官得微清，則勝於轉。

translations.literal: Offices were judged only as pure or impure; advancing from an impure office to a slightly pure one was better than a lateral transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were judged only as pure or impure; advancing from an impure office to a slightly pure one was better than a lateral transfer, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 若有遷授，或由別敕，但移轉一人為官，則諸官多須改動。

translations.literal: If there was transfer and appointment, it might come through a separate edict; but moving one person to an office often required many other offices to be changed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Where there was transfer and appointment, it might come through a separate edict; but moving one person to an office often required many other offices to be changed as well.

sentences.zh: 其用官式，吏部先為白牒，錄數十人名，吏部尚書與參掌人共署奏。

translations.literal: The method of appointment: the Ministry of Personnel first prepared a white document listing several dozen names; the Minister of Personnel and the participating official jointly signed a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The method of appointment—the Ministry of Personnel first prepared a white document listing several dozen names; the Minister of Personnel and the participating official jointly signed a memorial.

sentences.zh: 敕或可或不可。

translations.literal: The edict might approve or not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The edict might approve or not approve, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其不用者，更銓量奏請。

translations.literal: If not used, another selection was weighed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Where not used, another selection was weighed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 若敕可，則付選，更色別，量貴賤，內外分之，隨才補用。

translations.literal: If the edict approved, it was sent to the selection office, further distinguished by color, measuring noble and base, divided inner and outer, and filled according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: Where the edict approved, it was sent to the selection office, further distinguished by color, measuring noble and base, divided inner and outer, and filled according to talent.

sentences.zh: 以黃紙錄名，八座通署，奏可，即出付典名。

translations.literal: Names were copied on yellow paper, jointly signed by the Eight Seats, submitted for approval, and then sent out to the registry office.
translations.idiomatic: Names were copied on yellow paper, jointly signed by the Eight Seats, submitted for approval, and then sent out to the registry office, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 而典以名貼鶴頭板，整威儀，送往得官之家。

translations.literal: The registry office pasted the names on crane-head boards, arranged ceremonial dignity, and sent them to the households of those receiving office.
translations.idiomatic: The registry office pasted the names on crane-head boards, arranged ceremonial dignity, and sent them to the households of those receiving office, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 其有特發詔授官者，即宣付詔誥局，作詔章草奏聞。

translations.literal: For those specially issued edicts appointing to office, it was announced to the Edict and Proclamation Bureau, which drafted the edict text and submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: For those specially issued edicts appointing to office, it was announced to the Edict and Proclamation Bureau, which drafted the edict text and submitted a memorial, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 敕可，黃紙寫出門下。

translations.literal: When approved, yellow paper copies were issued from the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Upon approved, yellow paper copies were issued from the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 門下答詔，請付外施行。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretariat replied to the edict, requesting transmission outside for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Secretariat replied to the edict, requesting transmission outside for implementation, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 又畫可，付選司行召。

translations.literal: It was also marked approved and sent to the selection office for summons.
translations.idiomatic: It was also marked approved and sent to the selection office for summons, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 得詔官者，不必皆須待召。

translations.literal: Those receiving edict appointment did not all necessarily wait for summons.
translations.idiomatic: Those receiving edict appointment did not all necessarily wait for summons, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 但聞詔出，明日，即與其親入謝後，詣尚書，上省拜受。

translations.literal: Once the edict was issued, the next day they entered with their kin to give thanks; afterward they went to the Department of State Affairs, entered the office, and received appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict was issued, the next day they entered with their kin to give thanks; afterward they went to the Department of State Affairs, entered the office, and received appointment, as recorded here.

sentences.zh: 若拜王公則臨軒。

translations.literal: If appointed duke or prince, they did so at the imperial audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Where appointed duke or prince, they did so at the imperial audience hall.
